name: SHapley Additive exPlanations
description: SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) explains one prediction by sharing out the gap between that prediction and a baseline, usually the model's average output over a background dataset, among the input features. Each feature receives a signed score, where positive means it pushed the prediction above the baseline and negative means it pushed it below. The scores are Shapley values from game theory, meaning each is the feature's average effect over every order in which the features could be added, and together they add up exactly to the gap. Exact calculation is costly, so tools usually estimate the scores by sampling or use shortcuts for particular model types, such as a fast exact method for tree ensembles, and averaging the absolute scores over many predictions gives a global ranking of features. In a fairness use, the difference in average output between two groups is shared out feature by feature in the same way, showing which inputs account for the gap.

sample_claims.text: For each declined application, the features with the largest SHAP contributions to the refusal match the lender's documented underwriting criteria.
Across the validation set, administrative fields such as ward code and admission day contribute negligibly to the readmission model's predictions compared with clinical measurements.

The difference in approval rates between applicant groups on the benefits eligibility model is accounted for mainly by the documented eligibility criteria, and the share of the gap attributed to postcode and other proxy inputs is reported.
The explanation shown to each fraud analyst accounts for the whole gap between the transaction's risk score and the average score.

name: Permutation Importance
description: Permutation Importance measures how much a trained model relies on each input feature. For each feature, the values in a dataset are shuffled at random, which breaks the link between that feature and the outcome, and the model is scored again. The fall in score, for example in accuracy, is the feature's importance: a large fall means the model depends on the feature, and little or no fall means it does not. Repeating the shuffle several times shows how much the result varies. The method works with any model, but it shows what the model uses, not what causes the outcome in the world.

sample_claims.text: The fraud model's accuracy on held-out data falls sharply when transaction amount or merchant category is shuffled and barely changes when customer postcode is shuffled.
The diagnostic model's accuracy on held-out patients depends on established clinical risk factors and not on administrative fields such as hospital identifier.
The environmental monitoring model's forecasts are most sensitive to atmospheric variables that domain experts consider physically relevant
The recommendation-model audit reports performance changes from shuffling behavioural and demographic inputs under a stated metric, without treating small drops as proof of feature independence.

name: Mean Decrease Impurity
description: Mean Decrease Impurity (MDI) scores how much each feature contributes to a tree-based model, such as a random forest, by looking at how the model's decision trees split the training data. Each split sends cases into two groups, and a good split makes each group more uniform in its outcome, which is a drop in impurity, measured with a score such as Gini impurity. For each feature, MDI adds up the drops from every split that uses it, weights each by the share of training cases reaching that split, and averages over all trees. The scores are usually scaled to sum to one, so they show relative importance. Because they come from the training data, they describe how the model was built, not how well each feature predicts on new data.

sample_claims.text: The five features with the highest mean decrease in impurity in the readmission-risk forest are the clinical risk factors that the clinical team documented as expected drivers.
No identifier-like or many-valued field, such as customer ID or postcode, ranks in the top ten by mean decrease in impurity in the loan-default model.
The mean-decrease-impurity ranking of the delivery-time forest is stable across 20 refits on bootstrap samples of the training data, with the same top five features each time.
Three meteorological variables account for over half of the total importance in the air-quality forecasting forest, and the model documentation names them.

name: Coefficient Magnitudes (in Linear Models)
description: Coefficient Magnitudes explains a linear model by reading its fitted coefficients. Each coefficient shows how much the prediction changes when its feature rises by one unit while every other feature stays fixed, and its sign gives the direction. Because a coefficient's size depends on the units of its feature, the features are first put on a common scale, for example by standardising them or by multiplying each coefficient by its feature's standard deviation. The features with the largest scaled coefficients are then read as having the strongest influence on the model's predictions. This gives a global view of the model without needing a separate explanation method.

sample_claims.text: Before coefficient sizes were used to rank influence in the valuation model, inputs were put on a common scale and strongly correlated input pairs were merged or reduced to one, so the ranking is not a product of units or collinearity.
The credit-scoring model is a linear model whose standardised coefficients are published in its documentation, so a reviewer can trace each score to its inputs without a separate explanation method.

The direction of every input's coefficient in the readmission-risk model agrees with clinical expectation, and none of the five largest standardised coefficients changes sign across 100 bootstrap refits.
Rainfall and soil nitrogen have the largest standardised coefficients in the crop-yield model, and their confidence intervals exclude zero.

name: Integrated Gradients
description: Integrated Gradients assigns input features scores for a prediction relative to a chosen reference input, called the baseline. It evaluates gradients, rates of output change, at points along a straight path from that reference to the actual input. Each feature's average gradient is multiplied by its change from the reference, and the resulting scores sum approximately to the output difference when enough numerical steps are used. For text, the path runs through continuous token representations rather than discrete word identifiers, and scores can be combined into highlighted words. In a protected-term variant, the reviewer fixes before the run a list of words or columns that name or record a protected characteristic, and reads the scores those inputs receive: a large score shows that the output rests partly on the characteristic, but a small score does not show that the model ignores it.

sample_claims.text: The retinopathy grading model's referral predictions are attributable to lesion regions in the retinal image rather than to imaging artefacts, as shown by Integrated Gradients review of a stratified sample of graded cases

The attribution scores given to credit analysts for each decision sum, within a stated tolerance, to the difference between the model's score for the applicant and its score for the documented reference applicant
The question-answering audit records token attributions for the documented reference and uses low content-word scores to select questions for separate perturbation tests.

None of the identity terms on the fixed list ranks among the five most attributed tokens, against the all-padding baseline, for the moderation classifier's decisions on the non-abusive posts in the audit set
The loan-screening bias review records the attribution ranks of specified protected-characteristic words in the reviewed statements, relative to documented reference inputs.

name: DeepLIFT
description: DeepLIFT (Deep Learning Important FeaTures) explains a single prediction of a neural network by dividing the difference between the model's output and its output on a reference input among the input features. The reference is a neutral input chosen for the problem, such as an all-zero image or a blurred copy of the input. The method measures how far each neuron's activation is from its value on the reference, then passes those differences backwards through the layers in one pass, applying a rule for each layer type. A plain gradient (the rate of change of the output with respect to an input) is zero where the output has levelled off, but DeepLIFT can still assign credit there. The scores add up to the output difference and mean something only relative to the reference chosen.

sample_claims.text: The binding-site model's highest-scoring regions in the validation sequences coincide with known binding motifs, as shown by DeepLIFT scores against a reference sequence with background base frequencies
The chest X-ray classifier's DeepLIFT scores on its false-positive cases fall on lung tissue and not on image borders or printed labels, using a blurred copy of each image as the reference
For the audited landslide cases, the input layers with the largest DeepLIFT scores match the causes named in the field investigation reports

Each declined credit application is accompanied by its largest DeepLIFT scores against the documented reference applicant, and the reported approximation error of those scores is below a stated tolerance

name: Layer-wise Relevance Propagation
description: Layer-wise Relevance Propagation (LRP) explains a neural network's prediction by working backwards from the output to the inputs. It treats the prediction score as a quantity called relevance, then passes that relevance back through each layer in proportion to how much each neuron contributed in the forward pass. The rules for this redistribution are chosen to keep the total relevance roughly constant from layer to layer, so the input scores add up to the prediction apart from small amounts absorbed by bias terms and stabilisers. Different rules can be used for different types of layer. The result is a relevance score for each input, such as a pixel or a feature, with positive values for inputs that supported the prediction and negative values for inputs that counted against it.

sample_claims.text: On the audited sample of chest X-rays, the relevance for the pneumonia output lies mainly inside the lung fields and not on laterality markers, text or image borders.
For every audited credit decision, the relevance scores for the decline output are stored with the decision record, and they sum to the model's score within the stated tolerance.
In the reviewed true positives of the defect-detection network, most of the relevance falls on the defect itself and not on the background texture that differs between production lines.

Where the perception model misclassifies a traffic sign in the test set, the relevance map shows whether the evidence for the wrong class came from the sign or from its surroundings, and each case is recorded.

name: Contextual Decomposition
description: Contextual Decomposition explains why an LSTM, a neural network that reads text one word at a time, made a particular prediction. The user picks a word or phrase, and the method splits the network's output score into two parts: the part due to that phrase alone, and the part due to everything else, including how the phrase interacts with the words around it. Comparing a phrase's score with the scores of its parts reveals effects that word-by-word methods miss, such as a negation reversing the sentiment of the word that follows it. The split is tracked through the LSTM's internal gates, so the model itself is not changed or retrained. The output is a numerical score for each phrase examined.

sample_claims.text: In the clinical-note classifier, negated findings such as 'no evidence of pneumonia' lower the score for that condition, as the contextual decomposition of the full phrase shows.
Each removal decision of the toxicity classifier that is sent to appeal can be traced to named words or phrases whose contextual decomposition scores account for most of the output score.

In the news-sentiment model used for credit monitoring, the contribution of a sentiment word changes sign when a negation or contrast precedes it, and contextual decomposition separates the word's own effect from its context.

For the audited support tickets, the routing model's decision is not driven by any single trigger word: phrase-level contextual decomposition scores account for more of the output than the strongest single-word score.

name: Taylor Decomposition
description: Taylor Decomposition explains one prediction of a neural network by splitting its output score into a contribution from each input, such as each pixel. It starts from a reference input, called a root point, that is close to the real input but for which the network's score is zero. Each input's contribution is the slope of the score with respect to that input at the root point, multiplied by how far the input sits from the root, and terms that involve several inputs at once are left out. Finding a good root point is slow for large networks, so the deep variant applies the same idea to one neuron at a time and passes the contributions backwards through the layers, which gives rules close to those of Layer-wise Relevance Propagation. The result is a relevance score for every input that can be drawn as a heatmap.

sample_claims.text: For each audited decision, the deep Taylor relevance scores of the inputs sum to the network's output score within the agreed tolerance, so little of the prediction is left unattributed.
On the audited sample of chest X-rays, the deep Taylor relevance for the positive finding lies mainly inside the lung fields and not on markers, text or image borders.
In the reviewed true positives of the defect classifier, the highest-relevance pixels fall on the defect itself, so its flags do not depend on board labels or background texture.
The inputs given most relevance for declined applications in the credit network are affordability and repayment measures, not postcode or other fields that stand in for protected characteristics.

name: Sobol Indices
description: Sobol indices show how much of the variation in a model's output can be traced to each of its inputs. The analyst sets a range or probability distribution for every input and runs the model on a large, carefully designed sample of input combinations. The variance (spread) of the outputs is then split into shares. A first-order index is the share caused by one input varying on its own, and a total-order index also counts every interaction that input takes part in. A large gap between the two signals that an input matters mainly through interactions, and optional second-order indices show which pairs of inputs interact.

sample_claims.text: Our flood-model review reports atmospheric inputs' main and total shares of output variance under the documented independent input distributions.
The portfolio-model audit records first and total-order sensitivity indices, distinguishing main effects from overall interaction involvement.
Our clinical-model sensitivity review reports patient-input variance shares under the chosen distributions, without treating them as a decomposition of every source of prediction uncertainty.

name: Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations
description: LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations) explains individual predictions by approximating the complex model's behaviour in a small neighbourhood around a specific instance. It works by creating perturbed versions of the input (e.g., removing words from text, changing pixel values in images, or varying feature values), obtaining the model's predictions for these variations, and training a simple interpretable model (typically linear regression) weighted by proximity to the original instance. The coefficients of this local surrogate model reveal which features most influenced the specific prediction.

sample_claims.text: For the transactions the fraud model flags, the features that the explanation ranks highest are ones fraud analysts judge relevant to the flag.
Explanations of the same prediction, repeated with fresh random samples, name the same top features, so the stated reasons do not depend on chance.
The explanation for each high-risk patient prediction rests on recognised clinical risk factors and not on artefacts such as the recording site or record format.
The content moderation system provides interpretable explanations for individual moderation decisions without requiring access to model internals
Customers receive the main reasons for an individual automated claim decision, drawn from a local explanation of that decision and checked by a reviewer for plausibility.

name: Ridge Regression Surrogates
description: This technique approximates a complex model by training a ridge regression (a linear model with L2 regularisation) on the original model's predictions. The ridge regression serves as a global surrogate that balances fidelity and interpretability, capturing the main linear relationships that the complex model learned whilst ignoring noise due to regularisation. This approach is particularly useful when stakeholders need to understand the overall behaviour of a complex model through transparent linear coefficients.

sample_claims.text: The model's global behavior is approximated by a simpler representation that captures dominant linear relationships across all predictions
The credit scoring model's decision logic can be explained through consistent linear weights applied uniformly across all applicant evaluations
The diagnostic system's predictions are attributable to weighted combinations of patient features that remain stable across the entire population
The environmental forecasting model's feature influences are represented through simplified linear coefficients that prioritize robust patterns over noise
The complex ensemble model's overall decision-making process is captured by an interpretable linear approximation that reveals primary feature contributions

name: Partial Dependence Plots
description: Partial Dependence Plots show how changing one or two features affects a model's predictions on average. The technique works by varying the selected feature(s) across their full range whilst keeping all other features fixed at their original values, then averaging the predictions. This creates a clear visualisation of whether increasing or decreasing a feature tends to increase or decrease predictions, and reveals patterns like linear trends, plateaus, or threshold effects that help explain model behaviour.

sample_claims.text: The readmission model's average predicted risk rises with the number of prior admissions and does not fall at any point, as clinical guidance would expect.
The credit model's average predicted default probability falls as income rises, with no unexplained reversal at any income level.
The crop-yield model's average predicted yield peaks within the agronomically plausible temperature range and declines on either side.
The driving model's average predicted safe speed falls as visibility worsens across the full range of visibility values seen in testing.

name: Individual Conditional Expectation Plots
description: Individual Conditional Expectation (ICE) plots display the predicted output for individual instances as a function of a feature, with all other features held fixed for each instance. Each line on an ICE plot represents one instance's prediction trajectory as the feature of interest changes, revealing whether different instances are affected differently by that feature. This complements Partial Dependence Plots by showing heterogeneous effects across individual instances rather than just the average trend.

sample_claims.text: The model's feature-response relationship varies across individual patient subgroups in clinically interpretable ways
The prediction trajectories for individual samples reveal heterogeneous effects that differ from the population-average trend
The flood model shows distinct response patterns to rainfall intensity across different watershed characteristics
The loan pricing model's sensitivity to income varies across applicant profiles without averaging over these differences

name: Gradient Saliency
description: Gradient saliency (also called vanilla gradient saliency) is the simplest gradient-based explanation for image classifiers: it takes the gradient of the score for a chosen class (the network's output for that class before it becomes a probability) with respect to every input pixel, in one backward pass, to show which pixels that score is most sensitive to. The gradient says how much the score would change if that pixel changed slightly. The method keeps the size of each gradient and, for colour images, the largest across the colour channels, then shows one value per pixel as a heatmap. Because the sign is dropped, the map shows sensitivity but not whether a pixel supports or counts against the class. In a bias-diagnosis use, the maps are drawn for the errors of a classifier already known to err more for one group, to see whether the sensitive pixels sit on a cue linked to that group; the group-wise errors come from a separate check.

sample_claims.text: For the pneumonia model's confirmed cases in the validation sample, gradient saliency places the most sensitive pixels over the lung fields and not over tubes, leads or position markers, in at least the proportion of cases the acceptance criteria set
The plant disease classifier's gradient saliency maps for its misclassified field photographs show sensitivity concentrated on the leaf area and not on soil, trays or hands in the frame
Gradient saliency maps used as evidence for this classifier were repeated on models retrained with different random seeds, and the sensitive regions agree across runs above the stated threshold

On the audit images, the retrained doctor-versus-nurse classifier's gradient saliency maps place the most sensitive pixels on uniforms and equipment rather than on faces and hair, the cue found on its errors before the training photographs were rebalanced

name: Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping
description: Grad-CAM (Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping) draws a heatmap over an image showing which regions most raise a convolutional neural network's score for a chosen class, which need not be the one the model predicted. The last convolutional layer produces a stack of feature maps, each a coarse grid recording where one learned pattern appears. Grad-CAM takes the gradient of the class score with respect to each map (how much the score changes as that map's values change), averages it to give the map a weight, and adds the weighted maps together. It keeps only the positive values, so the result marks regions that count in favour of the class, then enlarges the coarse grid to the image's size and lays it over the image, so the output shows broad regions rather than pixels. In a bias-diagnosis use, the maps are laid over the errors of a classifier already known to err more for one group, to see which image region the model relies on; the group-wise errors and the training-data counts come from separate checks.

sample_claims.text: For the melanoma classifier's validation images, the Grad-CAM region for the predicted class overlaps the clinician-drawn lesion outline in at least the proportion of cases set in the acceptance criteria

For the traffic sign recogniser's misclassified test images, the Grad-CAM region falls on the sign face and not the background in all but a reported fraction of cases, and each remaining case has been reviewed
The land-cover classifier's Grad-CAM region for each class in the labelled satellite tiles falls on the matching surface type and not on shadows or neighbouring land

On the audit images, the retrained doctor-versus-nurse classifier's Grad-CAM regions fall on uniforms and equipment rather than on faces and hair, the cue found on its errors before the training photographs were rebalanced

name: Occlusion Sensitivity
description: Occlusion sensitivity shows which parts of an input a model's prediction is sensitive to. A region of the input, such as a square patch of an image, is hidden by replacing it with a neutral value like grey, and the change in the model's output is recorded, usually the probability of the class of interest. Sliding the patch across the whole input gives a map of how much the output changes when each region is hidden. A large drop marks a region the prediction depends on. The method treats the model as a black box, needing only its inputs and outputs, and is most often used on images.

sample_claims.text: The diagnostic system's classifications remain stable when non-pathological image regions are masked or removed
On the images examined, the crop disease classifier's confidence falls when leaf lesions are masked and changes little when soil or background is masked.
The traffic-sign classifier's confidence in the correct class falls sharply only when the sign face is covered, not when the surrounding scenery is covered.
The image classifier's prediction does not depend on watermarks, borders or other artefacts, because masking them leaves the output unchanged on the test images.

name: Attention Weight Analysis
description: Attention weight analysis reads the weights an attention-based neural network assigns to the parts of its input, to see which positions it draws on at each step. The weights come from an ordinary forward pass and are plotted as heatmaps, one row per output step or token. In recurrent encoder-decoder models, such as early neural machine translation or image captioning, each output step has a row over the source words or image regions, read as a soft alignment in which weight is shared across several source positions. In transformers, each attention head (one of several parallel attention units in a layer) has its own matrix at every layer; the analyst views these per head and layer, or averages them over many inputs to profile a head, for example by how much attention it gives each kind of token, or how often its strongest attention lands on a labelled relation such as a verb and its object. The heatmaps show where each step looks; on their own they do not measure how much each input contributed to the prediction, because the weights leave out what is done with the attended values and information mixes between layers.

sample_claims.text: For a sample of equipment-manual sentences, the recurrent translation model's source attention put its largest weight on the source counterpart of each translated technical term, and sentences where it did not were reviewed by a translator.

In the reviewed sample of alt-text captions, the share of generated object nouns whose attention fell on the matching object in the image met the release threshold, and captions that fell short were checked by hand before release.
The attention heads identified as linking drug names to doses behave consistently across discharge letters from both hospitals in the validation set
Phrases that attention maps suggested were decisive for the clause classifier were confirmed by an independent attribution method before being reported to reviewers

name: Factor Analysis
description: Factor analysis looks for a small number of hidden factors that explain why a larger set of measured variables, such as a model's input features, tend to move together. Each variable is modelled as a weighted mix of the shared factors plus a part that is unique to it, including measurement error. The weights are called loadings, and they show which variables each factor is built from; for example, several credit-history features might all load on one 'repayment behaviour' factor. Unlike principal component analysis, which summarises as much of the total variation as it can, factor analysis models only the variation that variables share. Analysts usually rotate the factors afterwards, using varimax (factors stay uncorrelated) or oblimin (factors may correlate), so that each variable loads mainly on one factor and the factors are easier to name.

sample_claims.text: The default-risk model's correlated inputs reduce to a small number of named factors that account for most of their shared variance, so its drivers can be explained at factor level.
The flood-forecasting inputs group into a few factors whose loadings domain experts recognise as physically meaningful drivers.
The number of factors retained, the extraction method and the rotation are documented, and the factor structure is stable when the analysis is repeated on a separate sample.

name: Principal Component Analysis
description: Principal Component Analysis transforms high-dimensional data into a lower-dimensional representation by finding the directions (principal components) that capture the maximum variance in the data. Each component is a linear combination of original features, with the first component explaining the most variance, the second component the most remaining variance orthogonal to the first, and so on. This technique reveals underlying patterns in data structure, enables visualisation of complex datasets, and helps identify which combinations of features drive the most variation in the data.

sample_claims.text: The feature space reveals latent factors that explain correlated environmental measurements without relying on predetermined variable groupings
The model's high-dimensional patient data is reducible to a small number of orthogonal patterns that capture most variation in clinical measurements
The financial indicators decompose into uncorrelated variance components that reveal which measurement combinations drive portfolio risk
The image representation preserves maximal variance through linear transformations that identify which pixel combinations distinguish between object categories
The customer behavior measurements organize into ordered variance patterns showing which feature combinations best separate distinct market segments

name: t-SNE
description: t-SNE (t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbour Embedding) is a non-linear dimensionality reduction technique that creates 2D or 3D visualisations of high-dimensional data by preserving local neighbourhood relationships. The algorithm converts similarities between data points into joint probabilities in the high-dimensional space, then tries to minimise the divergence between these probabilities and those in the low-dimensional embedding. This approach excels at revealing cluster structures and local patterns, making it particularly effective for exploratory data analysis and understanding complex data relationships that linear methods like PCA might miss.

sample_claims.text: The model's internal representations reveal distinct local neighborhoods corresponding to clinically meaningful disease subtypes
Similar customer profiles cluster together in the reduced representation while maintaining separation between behaviorally distinct segments
The high-dimensional embedding space exhibits locally coherent structure that corresponds to interpretable data groupings
The sensor data's local proximity relationships in the reduced visualization reflect genuine environmental similarity patterns
Complex gene expression patterns are rendered into interpretable clusters that preserve biological relationships between nearby cell types

name: UMAP
description: UMAP (Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection) is a non-linear dimensionality reduction technique that creates 2D or 3D visualisations of high-dimensional data by constructing a mathematical model of the data's underlying manifold structure. Unlike t-SNE, UMAP preserves both local neighbourhood relationships and global topology more effectively, using techniques from topological data analysis and Riemannian geometry. This approach often produces more interpretable cluster layouts while maintaining meaningful distances between clusters, making it particularly valuable for exploratory data analysis and understanding complex dataset structures.

sample_claims.text: The high-dimensional dataset's underlying cluster relationships are visualized while preserving meaningful distances between distinct groups
The data visualization reveals both local neighborhood patterns and global topology without sacrificing one for the other
The model's learned representations can be explored through low-dimensional projections that preserve the manifold structure of the original feature space
Complex dataset structures with non-linear relationships are comprehensible through two-dimensional visualizations that maintain topological fidelity

name: Prototype and Criticism Models
description: Prototype and Criticism Models provide data understanding by identifying two complementary sets of examples: prototypes represent the most typical instances that best summarise common patterns in the data, whilst criticisms are outliers or edge cases that are poorly represented by the prototypes. For example, in a dataset of customer transactions, prototypes might be the most representative buying patterns (frequent small purchases, occasional large purchases), whilst criticisms could be unusual behaviours (bulk buyers, one-time high-value customers). This dual approach reveals both what is normal and what is exceptional, helping understand data coverage and model blind spots.

sample_claims.text: The medical imaging dataset's coverage is characterised by both typical tissue patterns and rare pathological presentations requiring specialised attention
The credit model's validation set includes both representative borrower profiles and exceptional cases that deviate from standard lending patterns
The environmental monitoring system's training data reflects both common measurement conditions and unusual scenarios that test operational boundaries
The hiring dataset's representative candidates do not systematically exclude particular demographic groups whilst edge cases disproportionately represent minorities
The system's performance on atypical cases is documented alongside its behaviour on prototypical examples

name: Influence Functions
description: Influence functions estimate which training examples most affected a model's prediction on a particular test example. For each training example, they estimate how much the model's loss on the test example would change if that example counted slightly more or slightly less, which approximates removing it and retraining without actually doing so. The estimate combines the gradient of the loss at the test and training points with the Hessian (the matrix of second derivatives, which describes the curvature of the training loss). The output ranks training examples as helpful or harmful for that prediction; because the theory assumes a smooth, convex loss, for deep networks the ranking is approximate, pointing to examples worth inspecting for mislabelled or unrepresentative cases rather than proving why the model erred. In a bias-diagnosis use, the rejections of a group already known from a separate check to be rejected more often are explained one by one, to find the training records that drive them.

sample_claims.text: The training records most influential for the readmission model's errors on paediatric patients have been identified with influence functions and reviewed by a clinical data steward
No training record among the ten most influential for any audited declined application is a known data-entry or labelling error

For each false positive in the spam filter's audit sample, the ten most influential training emails were reviewed and the cause of the error, mislabelled or unrepresentative training data, was recorded
The training records most influential for the audited protected-group rejections were reviewed, and none comes from underwriting rules since withdrawn or from branches with a documented bias

name: Contrastive Explanation Method
description: The Contrastive Explanation Method (CEM) explains one prediction of a classifier, such as a neural network, by describing what is present and what is absent in the input. A pertinent positive is the smallest set of features already present that is enough for the model to give the same prediction. A pertinent negative is the smallest set of features not currently present that would change the prediction to a different class if they were added. CEM finds both by solving an optimisation problem that searches for the smallest change to the input, and it can use an autoencoder (a model trained to reconstruct realistic inputs) to keep the changed inputs realistic. An explanation reads like 'this digit is a 3 because these strokes are present and because a short bar at the top is absent', since adding that bar would make it a 5.

sample_claims.text: For the invoices the risk model rates high, compliance reviewers judge that the pertinent positives are sufficient grounds for the rating and the pertinent negatives are events that would lower it.
For each flagged patient record, the pertinent positives and negatives match the findings clinicians use to tell the model's diagnosis from the nearest alternative.
On the instances tested, keeping only the pertinent positive leaves the model's prediction unchanged, and adding the pertinent negative changes it to a different class.
Each applicant declined for credit is told which absent factors, if present, would have changed the model's decision, and a reviewer has confirmed that each is something the applicant could change.
Caseworkers can tell an applicant which missing information, if provided, would change the eligibility model's outcome for that application.

name: ANCHOR
description: ANCHOR generates high-precision if-then rules that explain individual predictions by identifying the minimal set of feature conditions that guarantee a specific prediction with high confidence. It searches for 'anchor' conditions (e.g., 'age > 30 AND income < £50k') that ensure the model gives the same prediction at least 95% of the time when those conditions are met. This creates human-readable rules that users can trust as sufficient conditions for understanding why a particular decision was made.

sample_claims.text: The model's individual predictions are supported by verifiable sufficient conditions with quantified confidence guarantees
The lending system provides loan applicants with specific, actionable conditions that guarantee approval with stated probability
The diagnostic system's recommendations are justified by minimal sets of clinical indicators that ensure the decision under specified conditions
The hiring decision criteria are documented as precise if-then rules with empirically validated confidence bounds
The fraud detection system identifies sufficient feature combinations that reliably predict flagged transactions with quantified precision

name: RuleFit
description: RuleFit creates interpretable surrogate models that can explain complex black-box models or serve as interpretable alternatives. It works by learning a sparse linear model that combines automatically extracted decision rules with original features. The technique first builds tree ensembles to generate candidate rules, then uses LASSO regression to select the most important rules and features. The resulting model provides global explanations through human-readable rules (e.g., 'IF age > 50 AND income < 30k THEN ...') combined with linear feature weights, making complex model behaviour transparent and auditable.

sample_claims.text: The credit risk model's decision logic is expressible as a sparse set of interpretable if-then rules combined with linear feature weights
The patient risk stratification system's predictions are traceable to explicit clinical decision rules that mirror diagnostic reasoning patterns
The fraud detection model identifies risk through comprehensible rules that stakeholders can validate against domain knowledge
The customer churn prediction system's global behavior is approximated by a small number of actionable business rules rather than opaque feature interactions
The regulatory compliance model combines human-readable decision boundaries with weighted factors in a single auditable representation

name: Monte Carlo Dropout
description: Monte Carlo dropout estimates how uncertain a neural network is about each prediction. Dropout randomly switches off some of the network's units and is normally used only in training, but here it stays on at prediction time. Each forward pass (one run of an input through the network) therefore uses a different random pattern of units, and the input is run through typically tens to a hundred times. The average gives the prediction, and the spread across runs is read as epistemic uncertainty, meaning uncertainty from the model's limited knowledge rather than noise in the data. The method approximates Bayesian inference, but the spread is an estimate whose reliability should be checked against held-out errors.

sample_claims.text: On held-out chest X-ray cases, the classifier's error rate among the 10% of cases with the highest Monte Carlo dropout uncertainty is at least double its error rate on the remaining cases.
The fraud model's Monte Carlo dropout variance is higher on transaction types held out of training than on types it was trained on, in a held-out check run before deployment.
Object detections flagged as high-uncertainty by Monte Carlo dropout are missed or mislabelled more often than unflagged detections when recorded driving scenes are replayed offline.

name: Out-of-Distribution Detector for Neural Networks
description: ODIN (Out-of-Distribution Detector for Neural Networks) flags inputs that look unlike the data a neural network classifier was trained on, and it works on an already trained network without retraining it. A classifier reports a confidence score, the highest probability it gives to any class, but that score is often high even for unfamiliar inputs. ODIN adjusts the score in two ways so that familiar and unfamiliar inputs separate better. It divides the classifier's raw output scores by a large constant, called the temperature, before turning them into probabilities, and it nudges the input slightly in the direction that raises the score, which lifts familiar inputs more than unfamiliar ones. An input whose adjusted score falls below a chosen threshold is flagged as out-of-distribution, so its prediction can be withheld or referred for review.

sample_claims.text: Camera frames that fall outside the perception network's training distribution, such as those from a sensor fault, are flagged before the planner uses the network's output.
Scans that are not of the type the diagnostic classifier was trained on are rejected by the out-of-distribution detector instead of receiving a confident diagnosis.
The detector's threshold is set so that 95% of in-distribution validation inputs are accepted, and the share of out-of-distribution test inputs wrongly accepted at that threshold is reported.
Images of unfamiliar part types or from unfamiliar cameras are held for human inspection instead of passing through the automated quality-control classifier.

name: Permutation Tests
description: A permutation test asks how likely an observed result would be if there were no real relationship in the data. The tester shuffles the data many times in a way that breaks the relationship under test, recalculates the metric each time, and takes the p-value as the share of shuffled results at least as extreme as the real one. Shuffling the outcome labels and retraining tests whether a classifier's accuracy beats chance, and shuffling group membership tests whether a gap between groups in the rate of decisions, such as approvals, is larger than chance would produce. A restricted variant, Ojala and Garriga's second test, shuffles each feature's values separately within each class, which keeps every feature's own spread but breaks the relationships between features, so a classifier that makes significantly fewer errors on the real data than on the shuffled copies is using those relationships. The test needs no assumption about the shape of the data's distribution, but a small p-value does not show that an effect is large, important or causal.

sample_claims.text: The classifier's accuracy on the patient cohort exceeds what label-shuffled copies of the same data produce, at the 1% significance level
The new case-prioritisation model's accuracy advantage over the current model is larger than random swapping of their predictions produces, at the 5% significance level

The gap in approval rates between the two applicant groups is larger than random reassignment of group membership produces, at the 5% significance level, and is reported as a disparity to investigate, not as evidence of discrimination
On the validation dataset, the blood-pressure model's accuracy depends on the relationship between height and weight, not only on each taken alone, at the 5% significance level

name: Demographic Parity Assessment
description: Demographic Parity Assessment evaluates whether a model produces equal positive prediction rates across different demographic groups, regardless of underlying differences in qualifications or base rates. It quantifies fairness using metrics like Statistical Parity Difference (the absolute difference in positive outcome rates between groups) or Disparate Impact ratio (the ratio of positive rates). Unlike techniques that modify data or models, this is purely a measurement approach that highlights when protected groups receive favourable outcomes at different rates, helping organisations identify and document potential discrimination.

sample_claims.text: The recruitment system's job offer rates are statistically equivalent across gender groups
The automated lending platform produces approval decisions at equal rates for all ethnic demographics
The medical referral system assigns specialist appointments at consistent rates across patient age groups
The benefits allocation system provides positive outcomes at equal rates across protected demographic categories
The admissions algorithm produces acceptance decisions at statistically indistinguishable rates for applicants from different socioeconomic backgrounds

name: Adversarial Debiasing
description: Adversarial debiasing reduces bias by training models using a competitive adversarial setup, similar to Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). The technique involves two neural networks: a predictor that learns to make accurate predictions on the main task, and an adversary (bias detector) that attempts to predict protected attributes (such as race, gender, or age) from the predictor's internal representations. Through adversarial training, the predictor learns to produce representations that retain predictive power for the main task whilst being uninformative about protected characteristics, thereby reducing discriminatory bias.

sample_claims.text: The model's internal representations cannot be used to infer protected characteristics of individuals
The hiring system's learned features maintain predictive power for job suitability whilst being statistically independent of candidate gender
The credit scoring model's intermediate layers do not encode information about applicants' race or ethnicity
The diagnostic system achieves equitable performance across patient demographics without encoding sensitive attributes in its feature representations
The facial recognition model's hidden representations are uninformative about protected characteristics whilst preserving identification accuracy

name: Counterfactual Fairness Assessment
description: Counterfactual Fairness Assessment tests a model against the criterion of Kusner et al. (2017): a model is counterfactually fair if each individual's prediction would have had the same distribution had their protected attribute, such as race or sex, been different, with everything that attribute causes changed accordingly. The assessor first writes down a causal model, a graph of which variables cause which, covering the protected attribute, the model's inputs and unobserved background factors, and fits its equations to data. For each individual, the fitted model is used to infer the background factors from what was observed (abduction), set the protected attribute to another value (action) and recompute every input the attribute influences (prediction), giving a counterfactual version of that person. The model under test is run on the factual and counterfactual inputs, and the gap between the two predictions, per individual or as a distance between the two prediction distributions, is the evidence: distributions that lie on top of each other indicate counterfactual fairness under the assumed causal model. Every causal effect of the attribute counts as unfair, including effects that run through inputs it influences, such as test scores, which is what separates this criterion from versions that allow some pathways.

sample_claims.text: Under the causal model agreed with the admissions committee, each applicant's predicted first-year grade has the same distribution under their actual and counterfactual race.
Under the documented causal graph linking ethnicity, income and neighbourhood, the credit model's approval scores do not change when applicants' ethnicity is counterfactually altered.

The unemployment-risk model's individual scores are unchanged under counterfactual sex and migration background, given the causal model reviewed by labour-market researchers, and the sensitivity of that result to unmeasured confounding has been bounded.

name: Causal Discrimination Testing
description: Causal discrimination testing checks whether a system gives different outputs to otherwise identical inputs because of a protected attribute, by changing only that attribute, or a name, term or other proxy that signals it, and measuring how often or how much the output changes. Galhotra, Brun and Meliou (2017), who called the approach fairness testing, generate inputs from a description of the valid input fields, make copies of each that differ only in the protected attribute (for example, recorded sex), run them all through the system as a black box, and report the causal discrimination score: the share of inputs whose decision changes, sampled until it is known within a chosen margin of error and confidence level. For text, the same test substitutes identity terms or names in otherwise unchanged sentences, such as one religion or ethnicity for another, and reports the average change in the model's score across the substitutions, which Garg et al. (2019) call the counterfactual token fairness gap. Because every other part of the input is held fixed, the test needs no model of how the attribute influences other variables: it measures whether the system itself responds to the attribute, or to the chosen proxy. The output is a score per attribute and, if the tester logs them, the input pairs whose outputs differed.

sample_claims.text: Changing only an applicant's recorded sex changes the credit model's decision for fewer than 0.5% of last year's applications (upper limit of a 95% confidence interval from a random sample of them).
Substituting any listed identity term into non-toxic comments changes the moderation classifier's toxicity score by less than 0.05 on average.
Swapping names associated with different ethnicities and genders on otherwise identical CVs changes a CV's shortlisting outcome in fewer than 1% of the pairs tested.
The triage assistant's urgency rating changes in fewer than 1% of the vignette pairs that clinicians judged should be unaffected by the patient's stated ethnicity.

name: GAN-Based Tabular Synthetic Data
description: GAN-based tabular synthetic data generation trains a generative model on a real table, then samples new rows from it to produce a synthetic table that can be shared or used in place of the original. In CTGAN (Conditional Tabular GAN), a generator network learns to produce rows and a discriminator network learns to tell them from real ones. CTGAN suits tables through mode-specific normalisation, which treats each numeric column as a mixture of clusters, and through training-by-sampling, which shows rare categories to the model often enough for it to learn them. TVAE is a related model built on a variational autoencoder, another kind of generative network, rather than a GAN. The synthetic table aims to preserve the original's column distributions and correlations, and its rows are generated rather than copied, but this is not a privacy guarantee, because a generator can memorise and reproduce training rows.

sample_claims.text: The patient table shared with partner institutions consists only of model-generated rows, so no original patient record leaves the hospital's controlled environment
The external vendor built and tested its dashboard on a synthetic copy of the transaction table, so no real customer row was disclosed outside the bank
Every row in the published survey file was generated by a model trained on the restricted data, not copied from a respondent's record

name: Statistical Oversampling Methods
description: A family of data augmentation techniques that generate synthetic minority-class examples through geometric interpolation in feature space, addressing class imbalance problems that degrade classifier performance on underrepresented groups. The foundational method, SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique), creates new instances by interpolating between existing minority samples and their k-nearest neighbours. Extensions include Borderline-SMOTE (focusing generation near decision boundaries), ADASYN (adaptively weighting harder-to-learn instances), and SVMSMOTE (using support vectors to guide generation). These methods operate directly on feature vectors without requiring neural network training, making them computationally lightweight and applicable to any tabular classification task.

sample_claims.text: The training dataset has been balanced using SMOTE oversampling to ensure the classifier has sufficient representation of all demographic groups for equitable decision-making
The rare defect classifier has been trained on an ADASYN-augmented dataset that maintains the original feature distributions whilst ensuring adequate representation of all defect categories

The diagnostic model performance on rare conditions has been improved through Borderline-SMOTE augmentation targeting samples near the decision boundary, without introducing fabricated clinical relationships

name: Sequential CART Synthesis
description: Sequential CART synthesis creates an artificial copy of a confidential microdata set (records about individual people or organisations) that can be released in place of the real data, in the form used by the synthpop package for R. Variables are synthesised one at a time in a chosen order: the first is generated by sampling with replacement from its observed values, and for each later variable a classification or regression tree (CART) is fitted on the real data to predict it from the variables earlier in the order. Each synthetic record is passed down that tree using its already-synthesised values, and the new value is copied from a randomly chosen real record in the leaf it reaches, so the joint distribution of the data is rebuilt as a chain of conditional distributions. Disclosure risk is limited by setting a minimum leaf size, smoothing synthesised continuous values and removing synthetic records that reproduce unique real ones, and several synthetic copies can be released so that analysts can allow for the extra uncertainty that synthesis adds.

sample_claims.text: The research extract released to the project team was generated by sequential CART synthesis with a minimum leaf size of ten and smoothing of continuous variables, and contains no record that reproduces a unique combination in the source data.

No confidential microdata left the secure environment during model development: external researchers wrote and tested their code on a synthetic extract, and only the final approved model was run on the real data.
A disclosure-risk assessment of the synthetic admissions table found no synthetic record matching a unique real patient on the agreed identifying variables.

name: Federated Learning
description: Federated learning trains one shared model across several parties, such as phones or hospitals, without collecting their data in one place. Each party trains the current model on its own data and sends back only an update, such as the changed weights (the model's internal numbers) or the gradients (the direction of change). A central coordinator combines the updates, typically by averaging, into an improved shared model and sends it out again, and the cycle repeats over many rounds. Raw records stay with their owners, which limits how much sensitive data is stored or moved and can support data protection rules that favour collecting less. It is not a privacy guarantee on its own, because updates can still reveal information about the data behind them and the coordinator has to be trusted.

sample_claims.text: The model training process does not require patient data to leave individual healthcare institutions
The keyboard prediction model learns from user typing patterns without transmitting personal text content to central servers
Each participating bank trained the shared fraud-detection model without moving customer transaction records out of its own environment; only model updates reached the coordinator
The central server holds no copy of any participant's raw training data; it holds the shared model and, briefly, the updates it is aggregating

name: Differential Privacy
description: Differential privacy puts a mathematical limit on what a published result reveals about any one person. The data holder adds random noise, drawn for example from a Laplace or Gaussian distribution, to each answer before release, such as a count, an average or a table of statistics, so the answer would look almost the same with or without any one person's data. The amount of noise depends on how much one person could change the answer (its sensitivity) and on a privacy budget called epsilon, which sets how far the two cases may differ (the Gaussian mechanism adds a second, small parameter, delta, for the chance of exceeding that limit). A smaller epsilon means more noise, a stronger guarantee and less accurate answers, and each release spends part of the budget. The guarantee covers whether a person's data took part, not conclusions about the wider population that the results legitimately show.

sample_claims.text: The published census tables were produced by a mechanism satisfying epsilon-differential privacy with a stated epsilon, so adding or removing any one household changes the probability of any published output by at most a factor of e to the power epsilon
Weekly admission counts are released with Laplace noise calibrated to a sensitivity of one patient, and the total privacy budget spent across all releases is tracked and capped
The analytics interface refuses further queries from an analyst once their allocated privacy budget is spent, so cumulative disclosure about any one individual stays within the agreed bound
Aggregate spending statistics shared with a research partner carry a documented epsilon, which bounds how much the partner can learn about whether any one customer's data was included
The model performance metrics across demographic groups are accompanied by documented privacy budget allocation and noise parameters

name: Homomorphic Encryption
description: Homomorphic encryption lets a server compute on data that stays encrypted, so the server never sees the underlying values. The data owner encrypts the inputs, the server performs the arithmetic directly on the encrypted data, and only the holder of the secret key can decrypt the result. For machine learning, the model is first rewritten using operations the scheme supports, such as additions, multiplications and polynomial approximations of other functions. Exact schemes return the same answer as the unencrypted computation, while approximate schemes, often used for neural networks, return a close one. The guarantee is confidentiality of the data while it is processed, on the usual assumption that the server follows the protocol.

sample_claims.text: The cloud provider processes the hospital's patient records only in encrypted form and holds no key that can decrypt them
Individual-level genotype data stay encrypted at every stage on the analysis server, and only the aggregate association statistics are ever decrypted
A breach of the third-party hosting environment exposes only ciphertexts of the bank's customer data, because the secret key never leaves the bank
Encrypted queries sent to the hosted model reveal neither the client's inputs nor the predictions to the operator, even to an administrator with full access to the server's memory and storage

name: Quantile Regression
description: Quantile regression predicts chosen percentiles of an outcome, such as the 10th, 50th and 90th, rather than only its average. In the classical method a separate model is fitted for each percentile, using a loss that penalises under-prediction and over-prediction unequally. For example, instead of predicting an average house price of £300,000, it can predict that a house of a given size and location has a 10% chance of selling below £250,000 and a 90% chance of selling below £380,000. Comparing the fitted percentiles shows how features affect different parts of the outcome, such as size mattering more for expensive homes than for cheap ones. A low and a high percentile together give a prediction interval (a range expected to contain a new outcome) without assuming the errors are normally distributed, though how often the interval actually contains new outcomes must be checked on held-out data.

sample_claims.text: The flood forecasting model estimates the specified lower and upper conditional quantiles of river level without imposing a symmetric error distribution, and how often observed levels fall inside them has been checked on held-out events.

The 90th percentile recovery-time forecast exceeds the observed recovery time for at least 90% of patients in the held-out audit sample, so the quoted longest timeframe is not systematically too short.
The wind power forecast's 10th to 90th percentile band contains observed output about 80% of the time on out-of-sample data, in each of the low, medium and high wind-speed ranges.

name: Conformal Prediction
description: Conformal prediction wraps any trained model so that, instead of a single answer, it returns a set of plausible answers (an interval, for a numeric prediction) that contains the true outcome at a chosen rate, such as at least 95% of the time. It first scores, on a calibration set of labelled data kept apart from training, how unusual each known outcome looks given the model's prediction, using a nonconformity score, and for a new case it keeps every candidate answer whose score falls below a threshold taken from those calibration scores. A diagnostic model might then return 'cancer or benign tumour' rather than 'likely cancer', and with a suitable score the sets grow larger where the model is less certain. The guarantee is distribution-free, meaning it assumes nothing about the shape of the data, but it does assume the calibration data and new cases are exchangeable, roughly that they come from the same source in no particular order. It holds on average over all cases, not within each subgroup, unless the calibration is done separately within each predefined group (Mondrian conformal prediction), which needs enough calibration cases in every group.

sample_claims.text: On a held-out test set from the same patient population as the calibration data, the 95% prediction sets contained the true diagnosis in at least 95% of cases, within sampling error.
Prediction-set coverage on the latest quarter of live data stays within the agreed margin of its nominal level, so there is no sign that the exchangeability assumption has broken down in deployment.

For the perception model, the 95% prediction sets contained the true object class in at least 95% of held-out frames, and frames whose set holds more than one class trigger the cautious fallback behaviour.
Every credit-limit recommendation is shown with a set of plausible limit bands at 90% coverage, and any case whose set holds more than one band is routed to a human underwriter.

The 90% prediction sets are calibrated separately within each demographic group, and on held-out cases their coverage is within three percentage points of 90% in every group, with each group's number of calibration and test cases reported.

name: Platt Scaling
description: Platt scaling turns a classifier's raw scores into calibrated probabilities, meaning that among the cases given a probability of 0.3, about 30 per cent turn out to be positive. It was introduced for support vector machines, whose outputs are distances from a decision boundary rather than probabilities, and applies to any binary classifier that produces a real-valued score. After the classifier is trained, a two-parameter logistic (sigmoid) curve, P(y = 1 | f) = 1 / (1 + exp(A·f + B)), is fitted by maximum likelihood to map each score f to a probability, using labelled cases the classifier was not trained on, taken from a held-out set or from cross-validation folds. The fitted curve is strictly monotonic, so the order of cases and ranking measures such as the area under the ROC curve (how well the scores separate the two classes) are unchanged; only the probability attached to each case moves. The output is a recalibrated model, assessed before and after with a reliability diagram (predicted probability plotted against observed frequency) and with the Brier score or log loss (two measures of how far predicted probabilities fall from what happened).

sample_claims.text: After Platt scaling on a held-out year of loan outcomes, the default model's predicted probabilities agree with observed default rates in every score decile, within the tolerance set in the model risk policy.

After Platt scaling, the defect classifier's log loss on the held-out test set is lower than before, and its reliability diagram shows predicted defect rates within the tolerance set in the quality plan.

Each flagged claim is shown to caseworkers with a probability calibrated against held-out review outcomes, and the calibration curve and its meaning are published in the caseworker guidance, so a displayed 30 per cent corresponds to roughly 30 in 100 similar claims needing correction.

name: Temperature Scaling
description: Temperature scaling is a correction applied after training to a classifier that is more confident than it is accurate, a common problem in modern neural networks. It divides the model's raw scores (logits) by a single number, the temperature, before they are turned into probabilities, so a temperature above one lowers confidence and one below one raises it. The temperature is fitted on a labelled validation set kept apart from training by minimising negative log-likelihood, a measure that penalises confident wrong answers, and the model's own weights are not changed. Because dividing by one positive number never changes which class scores highest, predictions and accuracy stay the same. Stated confidence usually moves much closer to observed accuracy on data like the validation set, which a reliability diagram (a chart of stated confidence against how often the model was right) can show, but some miscalibration remains.

sample_claims.text: On a test set not used to fit the temperature, the diagnostic model's expected calibration error is below the agreed threshold, and observed accuracy in each confidence band is within tolerance of its stated confidence.

Calibrating the credit risk model with a single temperature left its predicted classes, and therefore its accuracy, unchanged, while its default probabilities now track the observed default rates on held-out data.
A displayed confidence of 80% corresponds to about 80 correct predictions in 100, as shown by a reliability diagram on data not used to fit the temperature.
After refitting the temperature on a labelled sample from the new region, the land-cover classifier's calibration error on that region's test data is no worse than on the original region.

name: Deep Ensembles
description: Deep ensembles estimate how uncertain a neural network's predictions are by training several copies of the same network independently and comparing what they predict. Each copy starts from different random initial weights, sees the training data in a different random order, and is trained to output a full predictive distribution, such as a probability for each class or a predicted value with its spread, rather than a single answer. The ensemble's prediction is the average of its members. Where members agree the prediction is usually more reliable, though agreement alone is no guarantee, and where they disagree the model is showing uncertainty about which answer is right, known as epistemic or model uncertainty. In the original study, ensembles of about five networks were better calibrated than single networks, meaning their stated confidence matched how often they were right, and expressed higher uncertainty on inputs from classes absent from the training data.

sample_claims.text: On held-out scans, the imaging model's ensemble uncertainty is higher for cases it gets wrong than for cases it gets right, so scans above the uncertainty threshold can be sent for manual review.
The ensemble's predicted probabilities are calibrated on held-out data, so that predictions made with 90% confidence are correct about 90% of the time.
When shown inputs from a class absent from the training data, the ensemble's disagreement is measurably higher than on in-distribution inputs, as tested on a held-out set of unseen-class examples.

The driving system reports an uncertainty level with each detection, derived from disagreement between independently trained networks, and remote operators are alerted when it passes the documented limit.
Each credit score shown to underwriters carries an uncertainty range from the ensemble, and scores with a wide range are labelled as low-confidence.

name: Bootstrap Ensembles
description: Bootstrap ensembles estimate how much a model's predictions depend on the particular sample of data it was trained on. The training set is resampled with replacement many times, each resample (a bootstrap replicate) holding as many cases as the original so that some cases are repeated and others left out; one model is trained on each replicate with the same settings, and every new input is passed through all of the models. The spread of the models' predictions for an input, reported as a standard deviation or as a range between percentiles, estimates the uncertainty in the model's prediction for that input, and inputs where the models disagree are those the training data constrain least. The spread covers uncertainty in the fitted model only, not the random variation in individual outcomes, so an interval meant to contain a case's actual outcome must add an estimate of that noise, for example from the models' errors on held-out data. Putting a confidence interval around a measured performance score is a different procedure, which resamples the evaluation set and retrains nothing; see Bootstrap Confidence Intervals for Evaluation Metrics.

sample_claims.text: For each substation's next-day demand forecast, the spread across models trained on bootstrap replicates of the historical data, resampled in whole-week blocks, is reported, and forecasts whose spread exceeds the planning tolerance are flagged.
The flood model's uncertainty for each river gauge reflects how much its predictions change when it is retrained on versions of the gauge records resampled in blocks of consecutive days.
Each readmission-risk score shown to clinicians is accompanied by the range of scores produced by models trained on resampled versions of the training cohort.
The spread of the housing-need model's scores across bootstrap-trained models has been compared between applicant groups and is reported for each group.

name: Jackknife Resampling
description: Jackknife resampling, also called leave-one-out resampling, shows how much a result computed from a dataset depends on any single record. The result can be a model's coefficients, its predictions or a performance score; it is recomputed n times on a dataset of n records, leaving out a different record each time and refitting the model where the result depends on one. The spread of the recomputed results, after a standard rescaling, estimates the bias and variance of the original result, meaning how far it would move with a slightly different sample. Records whose removal moves the result most are flagged as influential, and may be outliers or data errors worth checking. The method assumes the records are independent and that no single record changes the result abruptly.

sample_claims.text: The readmission model's coefficient estimates change by less than a stated tolerance when any single patient record is removed, so no individual record drives the reported risk factors.
The jackknife standard error of the fitted rainfall-to-inflow slope is reported with the estimate, and the planning threshold lies more than two standard errors away from it.
The scorecard's validation report lists the loan records whose removal most changes its coefficients, so reviewers can see how far the model depends on a handful of loans.

name: Cross-validation
description: Cross-validation estimates how well a model will perform on data it has not seen, and how much that estimate depends on the particular data used. The dataset is divided into k parts called folds, the model is trained on all but one fold and scored on the held-out fold, and this repeats until every fold has served as the held-out set once. The scores are averaged to give a performance estimate, and their spread gives a rough indication of how much the result depends on which data the model was trained on. Common variants are stratified cross-validation, where each fold keeps the overall class proportions, and leave-one-out, where each fold is a single example. A large gap between training scores and held-out scores points to overfitting, where a model has learned quirks of its training data that do not carry over to new data.

sample_claims.text: Across ten stratified folds, the model's AUC varied by no more than 0.03 around its mean, so the reported performance does not depend on which records were held out.
The fraud detection model's recall on fraudulent transactions stays within the agreed band in every fold of the historical data, with no fold below the minimum acceptable recall.

With all preprocessing and feature selection fitted inside each training fold, repeated cross-validation shows the readmission model's performance estimate is not inflated by information from the test folds.
The readmission-risk model shows no sign of overfitting, with held-out scores on every fold within the agreed margin of its training score.

name: Area Under Precision-Recall Curve
description: Area Under Precision-Recall Curve (AUPRC) summarises how well a classifier finds the cases that matter when those cases are rare. Precision is the share of positive predictions that are correct, and recall is the share of actual positives that are found. Plotting one against the other at every classification threshold gives a curve, and AUPRC is the area under it, from 0 to 1. Neither precision nor recall uses true negatives, so a large majority class does not flatter the score as it can flatter accuracy and AUC-ROC. A model with no skill scores about the proportion of positives in the data, so the score is only meaningful next to that baseline.

sample_claims.text: On the held-out transactions, the fraud model's AUPRC is above the agreed acceptance value and well above the no-skill baseline set by the fraud rate
At the recall that clinicians require, the screening model's precision on the validation set stays above the level that keeps follow-up workload manageable
The updated defect-detection model's AUPRC on the labelled validation batch is higher than the current model's, with the no-skill baseline reported alongside

name: Safety Envelope Testing
description: Safety envelope testing checks how an AI system performs at and beyond the edges of the conditions it was designed for, so that failure modes are found before deployment. Testers first write down those conditions, called the operational design domain, such as the road types, weather, lighting and speeds a vehicle is built for. They then build scenarios that push each condition towards its limit and past it, and measure how performance degrades as conditions get harder, repeating runs where the system does not behave the same way twice. The results show where, within the conditions tested, the system moves from acceptable to unsafe behaviour. They support operating limits, safety margins and a point at which the system should hand over to a person or stop.

sample_claims.text: The perception system has been tested at and beyond the limits of its operational design domain in weather, lighting and sensor-coverage conditions, and the point at which it hands control to a human driver is documented.

The diagnostic model's sensitivity has been measured across graded levels of image quality and case complexity up to the edge of its intended use, and the level at which cases are referred to a specialist is set from those results.

The forecasting model's error has been measured under progressively more extreme weather inputs up to the documented operating limits, with the point at which accuracy falls below the agreed bound recorded.
The trading algorithm's automatic suspension has been shown to trigger in stress scenarios when volatility passes the documented limit, before position losses exceed the agreed ceiling.

The inspection system's defect-detection rate has been tested at the edges of the lighting, part-orientation and surface-finish ranges expected in production, and the range in which it meets the required rate is documented.

name: Algorithm Review Boards
description: An algorithm review board is a standing, multidisciplinary body inside an organisation that examines proposed AI systems or AI research projects at set points and decides whether, and on what conditions, they may proceed. The literature also calls these bodies AI ethics boards or AI review boards. They differ from an Institutional Review Board (IRB), which protects the human subjects of research, because they also weigh harms to the people a system will affect and to society. A risk-based triage decides which projects need full review; the project team then submits a written account of the system's purpose, data, foreseeable harms and planned mitigations, and members drawn from technical, legal, ethical and domain backgrounds, sometimes with people from affected communities, question the team and iterate on that account with them.
