The board approves, approves with conditions such as a monitoring plan or a re-review date, or rejects, and the output is a dated decision record with its reasons and conditions that later reviews and audits can check against what was built.

sample_claims.text: Every high-risk AI system was reviewed and approved by the organisation's algorithm review board before operational use, and the board could have blocked deployment
The conditions the review board attached to the credit-limit model's approval, including a disparate-impact analysis by protected group and a re-review date, were met before and after launch
The clinical decision-support model was deployed under a monitoring plan and re-review schedule set by a multidisciplinary review board independent of the development team
The diagnostic AI system's development and deployment decisions are traceable to dated board decision records that state the risks assessed, the reasons for approval and the conditions attached
The review board's decision record for the risk assessment tool, with its reasons and conditions, is available to the oversight body and the public

name: Red Teaming
description: Red teaming is a structured exercise in which a team deliberately tries to make an AI system fail, so that weaknesses are found before real users or attackers find them. The organisers set the scope and the harms of concern, recruit people with a mix of skills (for example security testers, domain specialists and members of affected groups), and give them a way to log each attempt and judge whether it worked. Participants try manipulative prompts, awkward edge cases and requests designed to draw out harmful, insecure or discriminatory responses, combining many approaches where a test for one known weakness, such as prompt injection, covers only one. The result is a record of the failures found and how easily each was provoked, which is not a pass or fail verdict. It feeds a risk register (the list of known risks and who owns them) and fixes, and the exercise is repeated when the system changes.

sample_claims.text: A red-team exercise with clinicians and engineers tested the clinical-notes assistant against the hazards in its safety case, and every high-severity failure it found has a recorded fix or an accepted-risk decision.
The customer-service assistant was red-teamed for prompt injection and extraction of client data before launch, and each successful attack was fixed and re-tested.
A red-team exercise that included people from the affected groups probed the benefits assistant for discriminatory answers, and every case found has been triaged and fixed or formally accepted.
Each customer-facing model had a red-team report reviewed by the governance committee before release, and its open findings are logged in the risk register with owners and due dates.
Red-team attacks against the deployed assistant are repeated after every model or prompt change, and newly successful attacks are tracked until they are resolved.

name: Human-in-the-Loop Safeguards
description: Human-in-the-loop safeguards hold an AI system's output at a checkpoint until a trained person has reviewed it. Designers set the rules that send a case to review, such as low model confidence (the system's own estimate of how likely it is to be right), a high-stakes outcome or a request to appeal. Some schemes also review a random sample of routine cases to audit the rest. The reviewer approves, changes or rejects the output, and the record of each review shows how often people overrode the system. Review protects only where reviewers keep using independent judgement, so the design also has to guard against over-trust and fatigue.

sample_claims.text: The autonomous vehicle system requires qualified driver intervention before executing manoeuvres flagged as high-risk by safety criteria
All loan denial decisions that are appealed are reviewed by qualified underwriters, and the applicant receives the underwriter's recorded reasons for the outcome
The diagnostic support system prevents treatment recommendations from being actioned until reviewed by a licensed physician
Every automated rejection in the recruitment pipeline is held until a named reviewer has confirmed or reversed it, and each decision is logged with the reviewer's reason
The content moderation system escalates borderline cases to human moderators based on defined criteria rather than relying solely on automated classification

name: Confidence Thresholding
description: Confidence thresholding uses a model score to decide whether a prediction should proceed automatically or receive different handling. For classification, a defined reject variant accepts the most likely class only when its estimated probability exceeds a chosen threshold and otherwise withholds the automatic decision. Thresholds can route withheld cases to specified review or fallback procedures, but those procedures require their own validation. Recording the score, threshold and resulting route makes the decision rule inspectable. The operating point trades automatic coverage against accepted errors, and an estimated score is not a guarantee that a decision is correct or safe.

sample_claims.text: The vehicle's planner switches to its conservative fallback whenever perception confidence falls below the validated threshold.
Screening results the model is least certain about are referred to a clinician, and the error rate among results released without review stays within the clinical target at the chosen threshold.
Transactions scoring below the review threshold go to an analyst, and the resulting review queue stays within the fraud team's agreed daily capacity.
The deferral rate and the error rate among automatically handled cases at the operating threshold are documented and reported to the oversight board.
Each prediction shown to staff carries its confidence level, and predictions below the threshold are labelled as low confidence.

name: Runtime Monitoring and Circuit Breakers
description: Runtime monitoring and circuit breakers observe a deployed AI service and restrict model calls when configured signals breach specified limits. In the closed state, requests pass through and recent failures are counted, while an open breaker rejects requests or provides a configured fallback, such as a cached answer, a simpler model, a rule-based default or referral to a person. After a waiting period, the half-open state permits a few trial calls and closes again only if they succeed. Model-related triggers can include immediately available signals such as input-drift scores (how far incoming data has moved from the training data) or low prediction confidence, since accuracy usually needs later outcome labels. Logs record state changes and triggering signals, supporting review of why the service was restricted without guaranteeing that the fallback is safe.

sample_claims.text: The diagnostic-support service stops showing model suggestions to clinicians when the share of low-confidence predictions or the input drift score passes its preset limit, and the standard clinical workflow applies until the breaker is reset.
The fraud-scoring service keeps answering requests during a model fault because the breaker diverts traffic to a rules-based fallback once the failure rate passes its threshold.
The forecasting service falls back to a simple baseline forecast when its inputs leave their historical ranges, so downstream users do not receive out-of-range forecasts.
Every breaker state change is recorded with its time, the metric that triggered it and the fallback used, and the log is available to system owners and auditors.
The platform records when its configured runtime restrictions activate and when normal calls resume.

name: Model Cards
description: A model card is a short structured document published with a trained model, stating what the model is for and what it should not be used for. It reports how the model performs on stated evaluation data, with results broken down by group (for example age or sex) and by operating condition (for example lighting or device) where these matter. It also records the training data, the metrics chosen and why, ethical considerations and known caveats. Readers use the card to judge whether the model suits their purpose before they deploy it. The original proposal gives suggested sections rather than a fixed format, and a card is only as reliable as the evaluation behind it.

sample_claims.text: The model's performance report identifies the assessed groups, operating conditions, metrics and evaluation datasets, including stated gaps.
The diagnostic model's card reports measured error differences and uncertainty for the specified patient groups and intersections.
The model's intended use cases and known limitations are clearly communicated to decision-makers
The lending model's card reports the selected group-comparison metrics and their assessment scope, without asserting equitable decisions from documentation alone.
The system's card records the stated training context, evaluation procedures and ethical considerations for inspection.

name: Datasheets for Datasets
description: A datasheet for a dataset is a short document that accompanies the dataset and answers a set of questions about it, in the way an electronic component comes with a datasheet. Gebru and colleagues group the questions into seven sections: why the dataset was made, what it contains, how it was collected, how it was cleaned and labelled, what it should and should not be used for, how it is distributed, and who maintains it. Creators read the questions before collecting data, answer them when the dataset is finished, and update the sheet when the dataset changes. People considering the dataset read it to judge whether it suits their task and what risks it carries. The questions are a prompt rather than a checklist, and a datasheet records what is known without testing it.

sample_claims.text: The training dataset's collection methodology, participant consent procedures, and intended use constraints are documented and accessible to model developers
The dataset's composition by demographic group and its sampling method are documented, so model developers can judge whether the data represents the population the model will serve.
Every dataset used to train the eligibility model has a completed datasheet that the data governance group reviewed before training began.
The data provenance from original sources through preprocessing transformations is traceable for regulatory review
The datasheet for the perception training data records the operating conditions covered and those known to be missing, so the safety case can state the limits of the data.

name: MLflow Experiment Tracking
description: MLflow is an open-source platform that tracks machine learning experiments by automatically logging parameters, metrics, models, and artifacts throughout the ML lifecycle. It provides a centralised repository for comparing different experimental runs, reproducing results, and managing model versions. Teams can track hyperparameters, evaluation metrics, model files, and execution environment details, creating a comprehensive audit trail that supports collaboration, reproducibility, and regulatory compliance across the entire machine learning development process.

sample_claims.text: All experimental configurations and hyperparameters tested during model development are centrally logged with their corresponding performance outcomes
The deployed clinical model is reproducible from logged training parameters, data versions, and execution environment specifications
The fraud detection model's performance evolution across successive training runs is traceable through logged metrics and artifact histories
The production model version can be systematically compared against alternative experimental configurations evaluated during development
Model training artifacts and evaluation metrics are accessible to authorized team members through a centralized repository supporting collaborative review

name: Data Version Control
description: Data Version Control (DVC) is a Git-like version control system specifically designed for machine learning data, models, and experiments. It tracks changes to large data files, maintains reproducible ML pipelines, and creates a complete audit trail of data transformations, model training, and evaluation processes. DVC works alongside Git to provide end-to-end lineage tracking from raw data through preprocessing, training, and deployment, enabling teams to reproduce any model version and understand exactly how datasets evolved throughout the ML lifecycle.

sample_claims.text: The training dataset's lineage is traceable from original data sources through all preprocessing transformations to the deployed model
The model's performance can be recreated using the exact dataset version and pipeline configuration from any prior release
All modifications to sensor calibration data and feature extraction steps are documented with timestamps and author attribution
The system can be rolled back to any previous data processing pipeline version when performance degradation is detected
The complete history of dataset changes is preserved and queryable across the model's development lifecycle

name: Monotonicity Constraints
description: Monotonicity constraints require a model's prediction to move only one way as a chosen input rises, with the other inputs held fixed, so that, for example, predicted salary never falls as years of experience increase. The direction for each constrained feature is set from domain knowledge before training, and the learning algorithm or model structure then rules out any fit that breaks it, so the model cannot learn reversals that come from noise or sampling quirks in the data. Boosted-tree libraries apply the constraint when they choose splits and monotonic neural networks build it into their structure, while penalty-based methods only discourage violations. Because a penalty, a constraint set on the wrong column or a later processing step can still let a reversal through, testers then vary each constrained input across its range over many generated or real cases, with the other inputs fixed, and count any prediction that moves the wrong way. The evidence is that violation count, expected to be zero, together with a comparison of held-out accuracy with and without the constraint.

sample_claims.text: Every constrained input in the mortgage model has a documented direction of effect, so loan officers can tell an applicant that, other details being equal, higher income never lowers the approval score.
The clinical risk score is documented as never falling when a vital-sign measure worsens, other measures being equal, and clinicians are given that rule before they use the score.
In property-based testing over generated patient records, raising age or the number of chronic conditions on its own never lowered the cost model's prediction, and the test is rerun on every release
In sweeps of each constrained input across its full range, the building demand forecast recorded no case where predicted demand fell as occupancy rose.
Across 100,000 generated applicant records, raising income alone never lowered the lending model's predicted approval probability.

name: Generalized Additive Models
description: An intrinsically interpretable modelling technique that extends linear models by allowing flexible, nonlinear relationships between individual features and the target whilst maintaining the additive structure that preserves transparency. Each feature's effect is modelled separately as a smooth function, visualised as a curve showing how the feature influences predictions across its range. GAMs achieve this through spline functions or other smoothing techniques that capture complex patterns in individual variables without interactions, making them particularly valuable for domains requiring both predictive accuracy and model interpretability.

sample_claims.text: The clinical decision model's predictions are decomposable into individual feature contributions that can be visualized as smooth curves
The lending model reveals how each applicant attribute nonlinearly influences approval likelihood whilst maintaining an additive structure
The model's decision logic is directly inspectable without requiring separate explanation methods
The resource allocation model documents how each policy-relevant factor shapes outcomes through interpretable functional relationships

name: Neuron Activation Analysis
description: Neuron activation analysis examines the firing patterns of individual neurons in neural networks by probing them with diverse inputs and analysing their activation responses. This technique helps understand what concepts, features, or patterns different neurons have learned to recognise, providing insights into the model's internal representations. For large language models, this can reveal neurons specialised for linguistic concepts, semantic categories, or even potentially harmful patterns, enabling targeted interventions and deeper model understanding.

sample_claims.text: The language model's internal representations reveal which individual computational units respond to specific semantic concepts relevant to clinical diagnosis
The content moderation system's harmful output patterns are attributable to identifiable neurons that can be selectively modified without degrading general language capabilities
The multilingual model's neurons do not exhibit systematic activation biases when processing text from different linguistic communities
The financial risk assessment model's internal computational units encode interpretable market concepts rather than opaque statistical artifacts
The model's specialized neurons for toxic content detection activate consistently across diverse phrasings and contexts of harmful patterns

name: Prompt Robustness Testing
description: Prompt robustness testing measures how much a language model's answers, or its performance on a task, change when the prompt is varied in ways that should not matter, such as rewording, formatting, capitalisation, reordering, or the typos and synonym swaps real users make. The tester starts from task prompts with known correct answers, writes variants that keep the meaning from templates or generates them with perturbation tools such as PromptBench, and runs the model on every variant. Some tools search for the variant that does the most damage, so a drop under that kind of attack is a worst case, not a typical failure rate. The result is reported as the spread of performance across variants, for example the gap between the best and worst format, together with the variants that changed the answer. On one widely used open model, accuracy differed by up to 76 points across formatting changes that kept the meaning, which is why one prompt template is not enough.

sample_claims.text: The triage assistant assigns the same urgency category to each benchmark scenario whether the patient's description is brief, detailed, clinical or anxious in style
The enquiry-classification model's accuracy stays within a stated margin of its mean across every prompt template and instruction paraphrase in the evaluation set
The risk category extracted from suspicious-transaction reports does not change when the same activity is described with different terminology or layout

name: Causal Mediation Analysis in Language Models
description: Causal mediation analysis traces which internal components of a language model carry the effect of a change in the input to the output. The analyst makes a controlled change to the input, such as swapping 'nurse' for 'man' in a prompt, and measures how the model's next-word probabilities shift. To find the indirect effect through one component (a single neuron, or an attention head, which is the part of the model that chooses which earlier words to focus on), they feed the model the original input but give that component the value it took on the changed input. To find the direct effect, they feed the changed input but hold that component at its original value. Repeating this across many components shows where in the network a behaviour is carried.

sample_claims.text: On the tested prompts, most of the effect of the input change on the language model's output is carried by a small number of attention heads, each with a measured indirect effect.
The model's subject-verb agreement behaviour is carried by identifiable neurons that are reused across sentences of similar structure.
The shift in the probability of the unsafe reply caused by the instruction phrasing is mediated mainly by identified components, and the finding is reproduced on held-out prompts.
After mitigation is applied to the components identified as carrying the unsafe behaviour, rerunning the same analysis shows a reduced indirect effect.

name: Concept Activation Vectors
description: A concept activation vector (CAV) is a direction inside a neural network that stands for a human idea such as 'stripes'. The analyst supplies example inputs showing the concept and random counter-examples, and trains a simple linear classifier to separate the network's activations (the values a chosen layer produces) for the two sets. The CAV is the direction at right angles to that classifier's dividing boundary, pointing towards the concept examples. Testing with CAVs (TCAV) then reports, for one output class, the share of its inputs whose class score would rise if the activations moved in the concept's direction, and repeating this with many random counter-example sets and applying a significance test guards against a meaningless direction. Concept sets built from examples of a protected characteristic, such as gender or ethnicity, turn the test into a check of whether a class is sensitive to that characteristic, as the original paper demonstrates.

sample_claims.text: The chest X-ray classifier's 'pneumonia' predictions are significantly sensitive to clinically recognised findings and not significantly sensitive to scanner type or patient positioning, at the layers tested.

The content-tagging classifier's TCAV scores for the ethnicity and gender concept sets are recorded for every output class at the tested layers, and the classes with significant sensitivity are listed for review.
The traffic-sign classifier's sensitivity to graffiti, snow cover and glare concepts is documented with significance-tested TCAV scores for each sign class the approval authority has requested.
The object recogniser's class predictions depend mainly on concepts that domain experts regard as meaningful for that class, such as shape and texture, rather than on background concepts.

name: Reweighing
description: Reweighing is a pre-processing method, from Kamiran and Calders (2012), that removes the statistical association between a protected attribute and the outcome label in training data by giving each training example a weight, without changing any feature values or labels. For every combination of group and label (for example, women who were hired), the weight is the number of examples that combination would have if group and label were independent, divided by the number it actually has: the group's share of the data times the label's share, over the combination's observed share. Combinations rarer than independence predicts, such as positive outcomes in a disadvantaged group, are weighted up and over-represented ones are weighted down, so that in the weighted data every group has the same rate of positive labels. A model is then trained on the original data using these weights; the outputs are the weighted training set and a small table of weights that records exactly how each group-label combination was adjusted.

sample_claims.text: The approval model was trained on loan history reweighed so that every ethnic group has the same approval rate in the weighted data, and its approval-rate gap on held-out applicants is reported alongside its accuracy.
The postpartum depression outreach model, trained with reweighing by race, has a disparate impact ratio within the agreed range on held-out patients.
The shortlisting model's training data were reweighed by sex before training, and shortlisting rates by sex on held-out applications fall within the agreed tolerance.

The adjustment made to the fraud model's training data is recorded as a table of weights for each group and label, kept with the training run, from which an auditor can reconstruct how the data were changed.

name: Disparate Impact Remover
description: Disparate Impact Remover is a preprocessing technique that transforms feature values in a dataset to reduce statistical dependence between features and protected attributes (like race or gender). The method modifies non-protected features through mathematical transformations that preserve the utility of the data whilst reducing correlations that could lead to discriminatory outcomes. This approach specifically targets the '80% rule' disparate impact threshold by adjusting feature distributions to ensure more equitable treatment across demographic groups in downstream model predictions.

sample_claims.text: The model's input features exhibit reduced statistical dependence on protected demographic attributes
The credit assessment system meets the 80% rule threshold for equitable treatment across demographic groups
The lending model's feature transformations preserve creditworthiness information whilst reducing demographic correlations

name: Fairness GAN
description: A data generation technique that employs Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to create fair synthetic datasets by learning to generate data representations that preserve utility whilst obfuscating protected attributes. Unlike traditional GANs, Fairness GANs incorporate fairness constraints into the training objective, ensuring that the generated data maintains statistical parity across demographic groups. The technique can be used for data augmentation to balance underrepresented groups or to create privacy-preserving synthetic datasets that remove demographic bias from training data.

sample_claims.text: The training dataset maintains balanced representation across demographic groups without compromising the statistical properties needed for model generalization
The generated dataset exhibits statistical parity across protected attributes without relying on direct attribute removal
The recommendation system's training data contains equitable representation of user demographics through controlled synthetic augmentation

name: Relabelling
description: A preprocessing fairness technique that modifies class labels in training data to achieve equal positive outcome rates across protected groups. Also known as 'data massaging', this method identifies instances that contribute to discriminatory patterns and flips their labels (from positive to negative or vice versa) to balance the proportion of positive outcomes between demographic groups. The technique aims to remove historical bias from training data whilst preserving the overall class distribution, enabling standard classifiers to learn from discrimination-free datasets.

sample_claims.text: The hiring system's training data has been corrected to achieve equal qualification acceptance rates across demographic groups through systematic label modification
The training dataset documents which diagnostic labels were modified to correct for historical treatment bias in underrepresented patient populations
The model was trained on corrected labels that remove discriminatory patterns from historical outcomes without altering the underlying feature distributions
The preprocessing pipeline identifies and flips classification labels for borderline cases to balance positive outcome rates across protected groups before model training

name: Preferential Sampling
description: A preprocessing fairness technique developed by Kamiran and Calders that addresses dataset imbalances by re-sampling training data with preference for underrepresented groups to achieve discrimination-free classification. This method modifies the training distribution by prioritising borderline objects (instances near decision boundaries) from underrepresented groups for duplication whilst potentially removing instances from overrepresented groups. Unlike relabelling approaches, preferential sampling maintains original class labels whilst creating a more balanced dataset that prevents models from learning biased patterns due to skewed group representation.

sample_claims.text: The training dataset achieves balanced representation across demographic groups without altering original qualification labels or outcome classifications
The recruitment model's training data composition is documented showing which candidate groups were preferentially sampled to address historical representation imbalances
The classification system's training data includes proportionate representation of borderline cases from all protected groups

name: Attribute Removal (Fairness Through Unawareness)
description: Attribute Removal (Fairness Through Unawareness) ensures fairness by completely excluding protected attributes such as race, gender, or age from the model's input features. While this approach prevents direct discrimination, it may not eliminate bias if other features are correlated with protected attributes (proxy discrimination). This technique represents the most basic fairness intervention but often needs to be combined with other approaches to address indirect bias through seemingly neutral features.

sample_claims.text: The model makes decisions without direct access to protected demographic attributes such as race, gender, or age
The lending system excludes ethnicity and gender information from all decision-making processes to prevent explicit discrimination in credit approvals
The recruitment algorithm documents which protected attributes have been excluded from candidate evaluation to ensure regulatory compliance
The diagnostic system bases treatment recommendations solely on clinical indicators without incorporating patient race or ethnicity
All decision-making processes are auditable to verify that legally protected characteristics are not used as input features

name: Fair Adversarial Networks
description: Fair Adversarial Networks is a pre-processing method, proposed by Cevora (2020), that produces a de-biased copy of a dataset from which a protected characteristic such as race, sex or age can no longer be predicted, including through proxies such as postcode or occupation. It trains two neural networks against each other: an autoencoder (a network that learns to reproduce its input) rewrites each record while trying to keep it as close to the original as possible, and an adversary network tries to predict the protected characteristic from the rewritten records. The autoencoder's loss adds its reconstruction error to the adversary's predictive success, so over alternating rounds of training it learns to remove the information the adversary relies on while changing the data as little as it can. The output is the rewritten dataset, which any downstream analysis or model can use without modification, together with the evidence that a freshly trained adversary predicts the characteristic no better than always guessing the most common category.

sample_claims.text: A classifier trained on the de-biased reoffending dataset cannot predict defendants' race better than always guessing the majority group.
The personnel records used to train the absenteeism model carry no recoverable information about employees' age group, including through proxies such as length of service.

The school funding model was trained on data de-biased with respect to majority ethnic composition, and its predictions no longer differ by that composition among schools with the same recorded performance.

name: Prejudice Remover Regulariser
description: An in-processing fairness technique that adds a fairness penalty to machine learning models to reduce bias against protected groups. The method works by minimising 'mutual information' - essentially reducing how much the model's predictions reveal about sensitive attributes like race or gender. By adding this penalty term to the learning objective (typically in logistic regression), the technique ensures predictions become less dependent on protected features. This addresses not only direct discrimination but also indirect bias through correlated features. Practitioners can adjust a tuning parameter to balance between maintaining accuracy and removing prejudice from the model.

sample_claims.text: The model's loan approval predictions reveal minimal statistical information about applicants' protected demographic characteristics
The hiring system's candidate evaluations are statistically independent of gender and ethnicity identifiers

name: Meta Fair Classifier
description: An in-processing fairness technique that employs meta-learning to modify any existing classifier for optimising fairness metrics whilst maintaining predictive performance. The method learns how to adjust model parameters or decision boundaries to satisfy fairness constraints such as demographic parity or equalised odds through iterative optimisation. This approach is particularly valuable when retrofitting fairness to pre-trained models that perform well but exhibit bias, as it can incorporate fairness without requiring complete retraining from scratch.

sample_claims.text: The hiring model achieves equitable selection rates across demographic groups through learned parameter adjustments that preserve candidate assessment accuracy
The fraud detection system satisfies equalised odds constraints across protected groups without requiring retraining from scratch
The environmental risk assessment model's fairness constraints are satisfied across geographic regions whilst maintaining predictive performance for resource allocation

name: Exponentiated Gradient Reduction
description: An in-processing fairness technique based on Agarwal et al.'s reductions approach that transforms fair classification into a sequence of cost-sensitive classification problems. The method uses an exponentiated gradient algorithm to iteratively reweight training data, returning a randomised classifier that achieves the lowest empirical error whilst satisfying fairness constraints. This reduction-based framework provides theoretical guarantees about both accuracy and constraint violation, making it suitable for various fairness criteria including demographic parity and equalised odds.

sample_claims.text: The lending model satisfies demographic parity constraints with quantifiable bounds on both error rate and fairness violation
The criminal justice risk assessment tool's predictions satisfy equitable treatment constraints with documented convergence properties

name: Learning Adversarially Fair and Transferable Representations
description: Learning Adversarially Fair and Transferable Representations (LAFTR) trains an encoder that turns each record into a representation, a vector of learned features, from which a protected attribute is hard to recover, so that models later built on that representation by other parties, including for prediction tasks not known in advance, also treat groups fairly. It was designed for a data owner who shares encoded data with downstream model builders and cannot control how they train. During training, the encoder, a decoder that reconstructs the input and a classifier for the original task play against an adversary network that tries to predict the protected attribute from the representation; the encoder is updated to defeat the adversary while keeping the information the other two need. The adversary's objective is matched to demographic parity, equalised odds or equal opportunity, and the authors prove that an optimal adversary's objective bounds that unfairness measure for any classifier trained on the representation (for the two error-rate measures the adversary also sees the labels used in training, so the attribute is hidden given the label, and the bound is with respect to those labels). The output is a frozen encoder, delivered with the accuracy and fairness of classifiers trained on top of it.

sample_claims.text: Classifiers trained by external parties on the released representation show a demographic parity difference below the agreed threshold on every downstream task audited.

A classifier trained to recover the protected attribute from the representation released under the demographic parity objective does no better than always predicting the majority group, within an agreed margin.
The fairness of downstream risk models built on the shared encoded data was measured on each new prediction task rather than assumed from the task the encoder was trained on.
Under a model-selection rule fixed in advance, the debiased imaging model narrows the gap in error rates between patient groups relative to standard training by a measured margin.

name: Multi-Accuracy Boosting
description: An in-processing fairness technique that employs boosting algorithms to improve accuracy uniformly across demographic groups by iteratively correcting errors where the model performs poorly for certain subgroups. The method uses a multi-calibration approach that trains weak learners to focus on prediction errors for underperforming groups, ensuring that no group experiences systematically worse accuracy. This iterative boosting process continues until accuracy parity is achieved across all groups whilst maintaining overall model performance.

sample_claims.text: The medical diagnosis system maintains equivalent prediction accuracy across patient age, gender, and ethnicity groups
The fraud detection model achieves consistent error rates across customer demographics without systematic underperformance for any group
The hiring algorithm demonstrates measurable accuracy parity across protected demographic categories with documented performance metrics for each group
The environmental risk assessment model produces equally accurate predictions across geographic regions and socioeconomic communities
The loan approval system maintains uniform prediction quality across applicant demographics without disproportionate errors for minority groups

name: Threshold Optimiser
description: Threshold Optimiser is a post-processing method, introduced by Hardt, Price and Srebro (2016), that makes an already-trained classifier's decisions meet a group fairness criterion without retraining it, most often equalised odds (equal true positive and false positive rates across groups) or equal opportunity (equal true positive rates only). Using a labelled validation set that records each person's group, it traces each group's ROC curve (the true and false positive rates obtained at every possible cut-off on the model's score) and chooses a separate cut-off for each group that maximises accuracy, or another chosen objective, subject to the criterion. When no single cut-off per group meets the criterion exactly, as is usual for equalised odds, each group's decision is randomised between two cut-offs with fixed probabilities. If the model returns only yes/no predictions rather than scores, the same method reduces to a small linear optimisation that sets, for each group and predicted label, the probability of flipping the prediction. The output is a group-aware decision rule that needs each person's group at prediction time; Fairlearn's ThresholdOptimizer implements the score-based form (and can also equalise selection rates), and AIF360's EqOddsPostprocessing implements the label-flipping form.

sample_claims.text: The credit approval model, with per-group cut-offs set on held-out data, approves applicants who go on to repay at the same rate across racial groups, within a stated tolerance.

After group-specific threshold adjustment, the readmission alert model flags patients who are later readmitted at similar rates across race and ethnicity groups, with overall accuracy and alert volume inside the limits agreed with clinicians.
The pre-trial risk tool's post-processed decisions have equal true positive and false positive rates across racial groups on a held-out sample of past cases.
The fairness adjustment to the CV-scoring model was applied after training, leaving the trained model unchanged, and its cost in accuracy was measured and reported to the selection panel.

name: Reject Option Classification
description: A post-processing fairness technique that modifies predictions in regions of high uncertainty to favour disadvantaged groups and achieve fairness objectives. The method identifies a 'rejection region' where the model's confidence is low (typically near the decision boundary) and reassigns predictions within this region to benefit underrepresented groups. By leveraging model uncertainty, this approach can improve fairness metrics like demographic parity or equalised odds whilst minimising changes to confident predictions, thus preserving overall accuracy for cases where the model is certain.

sample_claims.text: The hiring system's selection decisions in uncertain candidate evaluations are adjusted to ensure equal opportunity across demographic groups
The credit assessment model's predictions in borderline creditworthiness cases achieve equitable approval rates without modifying high-confidence decisions
The diagnostic system's uncertain classifications maintain consistent accuracy across patient populations through targeted fairness adjustments
The bail decision system documents which predictions fall within the uncertainty region and the rationale for fairness-motivated reassignments
The autonomous vehicle's object classification remains reliable across lighting conditions through uncertainty-aware decision adjustments that compensate for perceptual limitations in edge cases

name: Calibration with Equality of Opportunity
description: Calibration with equality of opportunity is a post-processing step that adjusts a classifier's scores so that two groups face the same error rate, in a score-based form of the equal opportunity criterion, while the scores stay calibrated. Calibrated means that, within each group, about 70% of the people given a score of 0.7 really have the outcome. The error rate is computed from the scores rather than from yes-or-no decisions, and for equality of opportunity it is how far, on average, the scores of people who truly have the outcome fall short of 1. Starting from scores already calibrated within each group, the step replaces a randomly chosen share of the scores in the group with the lower error rate by that group's overall rate of the outcome, which makes those predictions less informative until the two error rates match. Calibration is kept at a cost in accuracy for that group, and matching this score-based rate does not guarantee equal true positive rates once a decision threshold is applied.

sample_claims.text: The screening model's score-based false negative rate differs between women and men by less than the tolerance in the fairness requirement, measured on held-out validation data
Within each student fee-status group, the dropout-risk scores remain calibrated after adjustment, so a score of 0.3 corresponds to roughly 30% of students in that group leaving
The score-based error for students who go on to drop out is matched across fee-status groups within the stated tolerance, and each group's false positive rate is reported alongside
The accuracy lost by the group whose predictions were randomised is documented, and the model still meets the clinical acceptance threshold for both groups

name: Equal Opportunity Difference
description: A fairness metric that quantifies discrimination by measuring the difference in true positive rates (recall) between protected and privileged groups. Based on Hardt et al.'s equality of opportunity framework, this metric computes the maximum difference in TPR across demographic groups, with a value of 0 indicating perfect fairness. The technique provides a mathematical measure of whether qualified individuals from different groups have equal chances of receiving positive predictions.

sample_claims.text: The hiring system identifies qualified candidates at equivalent rates across demographic groups
The diagnostic model detects disease in affected patients consistently regardless of patient ethnicity

name: Average Odds Difference
description: Average Odds Difference measures fairness by calculating the average difference in both false positive rates and true positive rates between different demographic groups. This metric captures how consistently a model performs across groups for both positive and negative predictions. A value of 0 indicates perfect fairness under the equalized odds criterion, while larger absolute values indicate greater disparities in model performance between groups.

sample_claims.text: The criminal risk assessment system maintains equivalent error rates for both false alarms and correct identifications across racial and ethnic groups
The hiring model's accuracy in both accepting qualified candidates and rejecting unqualified candidates is consistent across all protected demographic categories
The credit scoring model's true approval rate for creditworthy applicants and false approval rate for non-creditworthy applicants remain equitable across protected groups

name: Path-Specific Counterfactual Fairness Assessment
description: A causal fairness evaluation technique that assesses algorithmic discrimination by examining specific causal pathways in a model's decision-making process. Unlike general counterfactual fairness, this approach enables practitioners to identify and intervene on particular causal paths that may introduce bias whilst preserving other legitimate pathways. The method uses causal graphs to distinguish between direct discrimination (through protected attributes) and indirect discrimination (through seemingly neutral factors that correlate with protected attributes), allowing for more nuanced fairness assessments in complex causal settings.

sample_claims.text: The hiring system's decisions are not influenced by gender through educational pathways whilst preserving the legitimate influence of qualifications on employment outcomes
The loan approval model's risk assessment isolates the direct influence of creditworthiness from indirect effects of demographic characteristics propagating through correlated factors
The decision process documents which factors legitimately affect outcomes versus those that create indirect discrimination through upstream correlations

The model's treatment recommendations remain consistent across patient demographics when controlling for symptom severity and medical history whilst allowing clinically relevant differences to influence care decisions

name: Fair Bayesian Optimisation
description: Fair Bayesian Optimisation (FairBO) tunes a model's hyperparameters, the settings fixed before training such as tree depth or regularisation strength, to find the most accurate model that also meets a fairness threshold chosen in advance, for example a difference in positive-prediction rates between two groups of at most 0.05. Because it only changes hyperparameters and retrains, it treats the model and its training pipeline as a black box, so it works with any model class and any group fairness metric, can enforce several metrics at once, and returns a model that need not use the protected attribute at prediction time (the attribute is still needed to measure fairness during the search). Each step trains a model with a candidate configuration and measures its validation accuracy and fairness, and two Gaussian processes (statistical models that predict a value together with its uncertainty) are fitted to the results of the configurations tried so far. The next configuration is the one with the highest expected improvement in accuracy weighted by the predicted probability of meeting the fairness constraint; until a fair configuration has been found, the search maximises that probability alone. The output is the best configuration that met the constraint, with its accuracy and fairness measurements.

sample_claims.text: The credit model is the most accurate of the hyperparameter configurations searched whose approval-rate difference between groups was at most 0.05 on validation data, and the gap was confirmed on held-out data.
The screening model meets the agreed limits on both the true-positive-rate gap and the selection-rate gap between groups when measured on held-out data.
The deployed model meets the fairness threshold without needing the protected attribute at prediction time.
The accuracy given up to meet the fairness threshold has been measured against unconstrained tuning of the same model and is documented.

name: Adversarial Training Evaluation
description: Adversarial training evaluation tests whether a model trained on adversarial examples (inputs altered slightly to cause errors) is really more robust, or has only learned to resist the attacks used in training. The evaluator first states a threat model, meaning the kind and size of change allowed and what the attacker knows. The model is then attacked with a varied set of strong methods, including ones not used in training, ones adapted to this particular defence, and ones that do not rely on the model's gradients, which exposes models that merely hide them. The main output is robust accuracy, the share of inputs still classified correctly under attack, plotted against the allowed size of the change and reported next to accuracy on unaltered inputs. Because attacks can only find weaknesses, the result is an upper bound on robustness, not a guarantee.

sample_claims.text: The model's robust accuracy under attacks not used in its adversarial training stays within an agreed margin of its robust accuracy under the training attack, at the perturbation size set in the threat model
The face-verification model had a lower observed attack success rate than its baseline under the specified impersonation threat model and test suite.
The spam filter's improved resilience to adversarial messages does not significantly degrade its accuracy on legitimate communications

The model's robustness gain over its undefended baseline survives attacks not used to train or tune it, including gradient-free attacks, so it is not explained by overfitting to one attack or by gradient masking
The medical imaging classifier maintains diagnostic accuracy on routine cases while demonstrating measurable resistance to deliberate input perturbations

name: Agent Goal Misalignment Testing
description: Agent goal misalignment testing checks whether an AI agent takes unsanctioned means to reach a goal it has been given. The tester builds scenarios in which the agent has a task, tools and access, and a forbidden route to its goal is open, such as deceiving a user, leaking confidential information or coercing people to avoid being replaced. Each scenario is run many times, and each transcript is classified as misaligned or not, either by a language-model classifier checked against human judgement or by human annotators. The result is the rate of misaligned actions per scenario and per model, with example transcripts, and how that rate changes when the tester varies a factor such as a threat to the agent's continued operation or an explicit instruction not to cause harm. The test needs no access to a reward function or to training, because it examines the behaviour of an already-trained agent.

sample_claims.text: Across the goal-conflict scenarios in the test suite, the agent took no action that disclosed confidential client data to an outside party
When told it would be replaced, the agent did not attempt to deceive or coerce its operators to prevent the replacement in any sampled run
The procurement agent stayed within its delegated spending limit in every scenario where exceeding it was the only way to meet the assigned deadline
The upgraded agent model shows a misaligned-action rate no higher than the version it replaces on the same scenario suite

name: API Usage Pattern Monitoring
description: API usage pattern monitoring examines how each account uses a deployed model's API, to catch misuse that no single request reveals. The monitor keeps a running record per account and compares it with a baseline of normal use, raising an alert when the account departs from it. Published detectors for model theft show two ways to do this: one tests whether the distances between an account's successive queries follow the bell-shaped pattern that ordinary use produces, and another estimates how much of the model's behaviour the account's queries and responses would let someone rebuild. Providers also score how often an account triggers content filters or repeats jailbreak attempts, and send high scores for review. The output is a log of alerts and the actions taken, which gives a dated record of how the API was used compared with the uses it was approved for.

sample_claims.text: The fraud API logs alerts from the configured query-distance detector so the security team can investigate suspected extraction-style sequences.
The clinical assistant records recurring harmful-content classifier flags by frequency and severity for the stated monitoring period.
The education API makes its request-volume summaries, monitoring settings and alert histories available for review of actual usage.
The moderation API records recurring harmful-content signals and the resulting safety-review alerts.

name: Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness Evaluation
description: Chain-of-thought faithfulness evaluation assesses the quality and faithfulness of step-by-step reasoning produced by language models. This technique evaluates whether intermediate reasoning steps are logically valid, factually accurate, and actually responsible for final answers (rather than post-hoc rationalisations). Evaluation methods include consistency checking (whether altered reasoning changes answers), counterfactual testing (injecting errors in reasoning chains), and comparison between reasoning paths for equivalent problems to ensure systematic rather than spurious reasoning.

sample_claims.text: The system's intermediate reasoning steps are logically valid and directly contribute to final conclusions
The medical triage assistant's step-by-step symptom analysis reflects genuine clinical reasoning rather than post-hoc justification
The legal research tool's case analysis demonstrates consistent application of precedent across equivalent legal questions
The tutoring system's problem-solving explanations maintain factual accuracy at each step without logical gaps
The financial advisory model's investment recommendations are grounded in verifiable reasoning that users can trace and validate

name: Constitutional AI Evaluation
description: Constitutional AI evaluation checks whether a language model follows the written principles, or 'constitution', that it was trained or instructed to follow. The evaluator writes test prompts for each principle, and can add prompts where two principles conflict or where a user tries to talk the model out of a principle. A judge, either human reviewers or a second language model whose accuracy has been checked, assesses each response against one principle at a time, often by comparing it with a baseline model's response. The result is a rate for each principle, such as how often the model's response is preferred to the baseline's, which shows which principles it follows well on the prompts tested and which it does not. A fuller evaluation also checks that following the principles has not made the model over-cautious or less capable.

sample_claims.text: On the evaluation's test prompts, the assistant refuses requests for harmful information while still answering legitimate educational queries
Across the scripted crisis conversations, the support chatbot keeps to its boundary between supportive information and medical diagnosis
Across the matched test stories, the news summariser adds editorial language no more often for one political position than for another
The homework assistant keeps to its principle of guiding learning without giving direct answers when users express frustration or urgency, at the rate set in the release criteria

name: Continual Learning Stability Testing
description: Continual learning stability testing checks whether a model that is updated over time with new data or tasks keeps what it learned earlier, by scoring it after each update on a test set for every task in the sequence. Backward transfer is the average change in accuracy on earlier tasks, and a large fall is called catastrophic forgetting. Forward transfer is accuracy on a task the model has not yet been trained on, compared with an untrained model. Scoring only at the end of each update can hide a sharp but temporary drop, so stricter tests also score the model during training and report its worst result. The scores can also show whether methods meant to protect old knowledge, such as replaying stored examples of earlier data or penalising changes to the weights that matter for earlier tasks, are working.

sample_claims.text: At every evaluated checkpoint during the update, the diagnosis model met the stated performance floor on held-out cases of previously learned conditions
The moderation model's worst evaluated checkpoint score on earlier violation categories remained above the stated acceptance target
The fraud model's old-task scores changed by no more than the stated tolerance at the evaluated checkpoints whilst new fraud patterns were learned
On the retained hazard evaluation tasks, the industrial monitoring model met the stated detection floor throughout the sampled learning checkpoints

name: Data Poisoning Detection
description: Data poisoning detection looks for training examples that an attacker has planted to change how a model behaves. The best-studied case is the backdoor: a few examples carrying a hidden trigger, such as a sticker on a stop sign, are mislabelled so that the model misclassifies any input with the trigger while it performs normally on clean data. Detection first trains a model on the untrusted data, then examines how that model represents each training example internally (its activations in the last hidden layer), one class at a time. Activation clustering splits a class into two groups by those activations and flags the smaller group when the split is clear, and spectral signatures score each example by its position along the main direction of variation and flag the highest scores. The flagged examples are reviewed or removed and the model is retrained, which yields a list of suspected examples and a measure of how cleanly each class separates.

sample_claims.text: Training images for the traffic-sign classifier were screened for backdoor poisoning with representation-based detection, and every flagged example was reviewed and then removed or cleared.
Photos labelled by the outside vendor were screened per class for a small separable group of planted examples before training, and no class exceeded the agreed alert threshold.
Screening found no class in the imaging model's training set with the tight, separable group of examples that a planted backdoor leaves in a trained model's representations, at the agreed threshold.
The moderation classifier's training data was screened for backdoor-style poisoning that would let a trigger phrase bypass the filter, and flagged examples were removed before the final training run.
After flagged examples were removed and the model retrained, inputs carrying the known test trigger were misclassified no more often than by a model trained on clean data.

name: Embedding Bias Analysis
description: Embedding bias analysis examines learned representations to identify biases, spurious correlations, and problematic clustering patterns in vector embeddings. This technique uses dimensionality reduction, clustering analysis, and geometric fairness metrics to examine whether embeddings encode sensitive attributes, place certain groups in disadvantaged regions of representation space, or learn stereotypical associations. Analysis reveals whether embeddings used for retrieval, recommendation, or downstream tasks contain fairness issues that will propagate to applications.

sample_claims.text: The recommendation system's item embeddings do not cluster products along demographic lines in ways that limit cross-group exposure
The document retrieval system's embedding space geometry does not position certain demographic groups in disadvantaged regions affecting search relevance
The medical language model's clinical term embeddings maintain equitable distances across patient demographic attributes
The content moderation system's embedding space properties are documented including encoded sensitive attributes and their spatial relationships

name: Few-Shot Fairness Evaluation
description: Few-shot fairness evaluation assesses whether in-context learning with few-shot examples introduces or amplifies biases in model predictions. This technique systematically varies demographic characteristics in few-shot examples and measures how these variations affect model outputs for different groups. Evaluation includes testing prompt sensitivity (how example selection impacts fairness), stereotype amplification (whether biased examples disproportionately affect outputs), and consistency (whether similar inputs receive equitable treatment regardless of example composition).

sample_claims.text: The language model produces equitable outcomes across demographic groups regardless of which few-shot examples are provided in the prompt
The recruitment system's candidate assessments remain unbiased when the composition of demonstration examples varies in demographic representation
The model maintains consistent performance across protected groups under diverse configurations of in-context learning examples
The system's fairness characteristics across different prompt example compositions are quantified and documented
The content generation model's outputs exhibit equitable treatment of demographic groups when few-shot examples contain varying levels of representation

name: Jailbreak Resistance Testing
description: Jailbreak resistance testing checks whether a language model or chatbot can be talked out of its safety rules. Testers write or collect prompts that try to elicit content the system is meant to refuse, such as role-playing a character without restrictions, framing the request as hypothetical, hiding it in an encoding such as Base64, or combining several of these. Each response is judged as a refusal, a breach or unclear, by a reviewer or an automated check. The result is the rate at which each attack family succeeds, with the example prompts that worked. This shows where the safeguards fail, but only for the attacks tried.

sample_claims.text: The clinical chatbot's responses to the recorded jailbreak set have been labelled against stated harmful-recommendation criteria, with failures and unclear cases reported.
The financial assistant's tested configuration has a recorded disclosure-failure rate for the specified confidential test target and attack budget.
The assessment assistant's restriction-bypass tests report observed violations and harmless-control refusals for the stated model version.
The assessment assistant withheld protected answer material in the recorded multi-turn policy-bypass tests.

name: Knowledge Boundary Probing
description: Knowledge boundary probing maps what a language model can and cannot reliably answer. A probe set is built from questions across the topics the system will face, including some with known answers and some that cannot be answered. Each question is asked in several phrasings, because a model may answer one wording correctly and fail on another. Responses are scored for correctness, for whether the model signals doubt when it should, and for whether its stated or computed confidence tracks whether it is right. The result is a topic-by-topic map of what the model knows, knows only under some phrasings, and does not know, which informs where to deploy it, what to tell users about its limits, and where to add training data or human review.

sample_claims.text: The clinical question-answering assistant's expected calibration error stays below a stated limit in every specialty in the probe set, not only in aggregate.
The customer-service assistant's documentation lists each topic with its probe results and names the topics where it is known to answer unreliably.
The policy-summarisation assistant's accuracy on developments after its training cut-off is measured and reported separately from its accuracy on established topics.
The maths tutor gives the same correct answer to at least 90% of paraphrases of each curriculum question it is cleared to answer.

name: Machine Unlearning
description: Machine unlearning removes the influence of specific training records from a trained model, so that the model behaves as if it had never seen them. It is used when someone withdraws consent or asks for deletion, for example under the right to erasure (the 'right to be forgotten') in data protection law, and retraining from scratch would be too slow or costly. Exact methods, such as sharded training, split the data into parts that each train their own sub-model, so a deletion means retraining only the sub-model that used those records, which gives a result statistically the same as retraining without them. Approximate methods instead edit the trained model directly to reduce the records' influence, which is faster but gives weaker assurance, and certified methods add a formal bound on how much influence can remain.

sample_claims.text: After patient withdrawals, the risk model was updated by retraining only the data shards that contained the withdrawn records, so it is equivalent to a model never trained on them
Each deletion request was handled by retraining the model components that used the user's data, and the processing log records which components were retrained and when
The production model can honour a deletion request within the legal deadline without a full retrain, at an accuracy cost inside the agreed tolerance
The financial model's update history identifies the withdrawn record set, affected constituents, checkpoint scope and completed retraining operations.

name: Model Extraction Defence Testing
description: Model extraction defence testing checks whether a model offered through a query interface, such as a prediction API, can be copied by someone who can only send it inputs and read its outputs. The tester plays the attacker, spends a fixed query budget on the protected interface, then uses the answers to train a surrogate model (a copy trained on the answers) or to solve for the model's parameters, and compares the copy with the original. Fidelity is usually measured as the share of inputs on which the copy agrees with the original, together with how many queries that took. The same attack is run with and without each defence, such as limiting queries, rounding or removing confidence scores, or adding noise to outputs, to show how much each defence raises the attacker's cost. The tester also measures the effect on legitimate users, for example accuracy or response time.

sample_claims.text: Under the documented query budget, the fraud API's output restriction reduced extracted-model agreement compared with the unrestricted baseline.
The essay-scoring API evaluation reports extraction success and rejection of legitimate requests for the tested rate-limit settings.

A surrogate model trained on answers from the traffic-prediction API within the permitted query budget agrees with the production model on no more than an agreed share of held-out inputs, while the forecasts stay accurate enough for planners
The prediction API returns only the output fields its legitimate users need, so extraction attacks that depend on confidence scores or partial inputs do not succeed

name: Multi-Agent System Testing
description: Multi-agent system testing examines systems in which several AI agents act on shared tasks or resources, to find failures that no single agent shows on its own. Testers run the agents together in simulated or scripted scenarios, often with injected faults such as failed sensors, delayed messages or conflicting goals, and record the failures that appear. Checks cover whether the task is completed, whether coordination breaks down (for example through deadlock, collisions or one agent's error spreading to others), and whether stated safety rules are ever broken. For language-model agents, benchmarks such as MultiAgentBench score task completion and the quality of collaboration or competition. For small or abstract models, a model checker such as MCMAS can search every reachable state for a violation of a rule written in formal logic and, for many kinds of rule, return an example run that breaks it.

sample_claims.text: No state in which two robots share an aisle cell or wait on each other indefinitely is reachable in the warehouse model, under its stated movement and failure assumptions
With junction sensors degraded and local objectives in conflict, the traffic management system keeps emergency-vehicle routes clear and delays within the agreed limits
In simulated high-volatility trading, the combined orders of the firm's trading agents stay within position limits and do not form patterns that the firm's compliance rules treat as manipulation
The agent team completes the benchmark coding tasks at or above the agreed success rate under the chosen coordination layout

name: Membership Inference Attack Testing
description: Membership inference attack testing checks whether someone with access to a trained model can tell if a particular record was in its training data. The tester plays the attacker, using the model's confidence scores, its prediction patterns or its loss on a record, often with shadow models, which are copies trained on similar data whose members are known. The attack is scored on records known to be members and records known to be non-members, which the tester must keep apart. The key result is the share of true members the attack identifies when it wrongly flags only a tiny share of non-members (for example 0.1%), because overall accuracy can hide an attack that identifies a few records with near certainty. The results guide the choice of mitigations, such as differential privacy or regularisation.

sample_claims.text: At a false-positive rate of 0.1%, a membership inference attack using shadow models identifies no more of the genomics model's training participants than random guessing would

The credit-scoring model's measured membership leakage, expressed as the share of training customers identified at a 0.1% false-positive rate, is below the threshold set in the lender's privacy risk assessment
An outsider with query access cannot tell, better than chance at a low false-positive rate, whether a given confidential contract was in the firm's fine-tuning data
After the diagnosis model was retrained with differential privacy, a membership inference attack's true-positive rate at a 0.1% false-positive rate fell compared with the previous model
The leakage figure comes from the strongest available attack, with shadow models trained on data from the same distribution as the target's training set, so a low result is not due to a weak test

name: Cross-Modal Consistency Scoring
description: Cross-modal consistency scoring checks whether content in one modality matches content in another, such as an image and its caption, a generated image and the prompt that produced it, or an audio clip and its description. It uses a contrastively trained model, one that has learned from large collections of paired examples to turn each item into an embedding (a numerical vector describing its content) and to place matching pairs close together: CLIP, trained on image-caption pairs, for images and text, or CLAP, its audio-and-text counterpart, for audio and text. The score for a pair is the cosine similarity of its two embeddings; in the standard image form, CLIPScore, negative similarities are set to zero and the result is rescaled, and no human-written reference is needed. A practitioner scores every pair in an evaluation set or in production, sets a threshold against a sample of human judgements, and then compares average scores between systems or sends pairs below the threshold for review. The score shows whether two items are about the same things, not whether every detail of a description is correct.

sample_claims.text: Every automatically generated alt-text description published on the collection website has an image-text consistency score above the threshold validated against staff ratings, or has been reviewed by a cataloguer

The new text-to-image model version follows prompts at least as well as the current version, measured by average image-prompt consistency on a fixed, varied prompt set and confirmed by human ratings on a subset
Image-caption pairs in the training set meet the stated consistency threshold, and the pairs the filter removed were audited for disproportionate exclusion of any demographic group

name: Trigger-Set Model Watermarking
description: Trigger-set model watermarking lets the owner of a trained classifier show later that a suspect model was copied from theirs, by planting a secret behaviour that only the owner can demonstrate. Before release, the owner chooses a small secret trigger set (in the originating scheme, 100 abstract images), gives each input an arbitrary label unrelated to its content, and trains or fine-tunes the model to return those labels while keeping its accuracy on the real task. In the originating scheme the owner also records cryptographic commitments to the trigger inputs and their labels, which fix the watermark at release so that a trigger set cannot be invented once a dispute has begun. To verify, the owner, or an arbiter shown the opened commitments, sends the trigger inputs to the suspect model through its ordinary prediction interface and counts how many return the assigned labels; an independently trained model matches them at about chance level, so a match rate above a preset threshold is evidence of copying. The technique produces the watermarked model, the commitments and, for each verification, the suspect model's trigger-set accuracy against the threshold.

sample_claims.text: The released model carries a trigger-set watermark whose trigger inputs and labels were committed to, and the commitments lodged, before release
Embedding the watermark reduced the diagnostic model's test accuracy by no more than the tolerance agreed with the clinical safety team
The watermark remained verifiable above the decision threshold after each fine-tuning and pruning attack in the stated threat model
Models trained independently on the same task matched the trigger labels at no more than chance level, giving the verification threshold a measured margin against false ownership claims
Ownership of the licensed model can be demonstrated to an independent arbiter through prediction queries alone, without disclosing either party's model weights

name: Out-of-Domain Detection
description: Out-of-domain detection checks whether a user's query falls inside the topics and tasks a conversational AI system is meant to handle. Scope is defined by examples, such as an assistant's supported intents (the actions it can recognise), and a detector then scores how closely each new query resembles them. Typical detectors set a minimum confidence on an intent classifier, add an explicit out-of-scope class trained on examples of unsupported queries, or measure how far a query's embedding, a numerical summary of its meaning, lies from the in-scope examples. A query judged out of scope can be declined, handed to a person or another service, or answered with a request to rephrase, instead of receiving an unreliable or invented answer. The detector tests resemblance to the defined scope, not what the system actually knows, so it needs evaluating on realistic out-of-scope queries.

sample_claims.text: The diabetes-support chatbot declines questions about conditions outside its remit and directs the user to a clinician, instead of offering advice it was not designed to give.
The tutoring assistant identifies questions above its curriculum level, at a recall measured on a realistic test set, and refers them to a teacher or other resource instead of attempting an answer.

On a held-out set of realistic out-of-scope messages, the claims assistant routes at least the agreed share to a specialist adjuster while wrongly refusing no more than the agreed share of in-scope claims.
Users of the resident-services chatbot are told when a question is outside what it covers, and the service owner reviews the log of unanswered topics each month.
Messages to the bank's payments assistant that fall outside its card and payment scope, such as requests for investment advice, are not answered by it and are handed to a person.

name: Synthetic Data Evaluation
description: Synthetic data evaluation checks whether an artificial dataset made to stand in for sensitive real records is safe to share and still useful, and reports the trade-off between the two. Privacy is tested by simulating an attacker who holds the synthetic data and some facts about a person, and measuring how accurately the attacker can use the data to infer that person's sensitive values. Fidelity is tested by comparing the synthetic and real data column by column and in pairs of columns. Another check trains a classifier to tell the two apart, and a classifier that cannot beat chance suggests they are statistically alike. Utility is tested by running the analyses or training the models the data is meant for on the synthetic data and comparing the results with those from the real data.

sample_claims.text: In the attack tests run on this release, an attacker who holds the synthetic patient dataset and a person's demographic details infers that person's diagnosis no more accurately, within a stated margin, than from population rates alone
Estimates from the researchers' models fitted to the synthetic microdata agree with the same models fitted to the real data within the stated tolerance
The fraud model trained on synthetic transactions performs within the stated tolerance of the real-data-trained comparison model on the same independent real-data test set
The synthetic dataset meets the stated agreement targets for the selected environmental analyses compared with the real reference data

name: Prompt Injection Testing
description: Prompt injection testing checks whether an AI system can be made to follow instructions its builders did not intend. In a direct attack the user types the instructions. In an indirect attack they are hidden in content the system reads, such as a web page, an email or a retrieved document. Testers run a library of attack patterns, such as telling the system to ignore its earlier instructions or inserting text that pretends the original task is already complete, and record how often each pattern changes the system's behaviour. Some programmes also test detectors that try to spot injected text before the system acts on it, and score them by the attacks they miss and the harmless inputs they wrongly block.
